questions.q: Which of the following is the correct definition of data?
o: Collected facts about a topic or item
Software that controls the storage and retrieval of stored facts
A centralized and structured set of tables stored on a computer system
The result of combining, comparing, and performing calculations on facts
questions.e: Data means raw collected facts about a topic or item. Combining, comparing, and calculating on those facts produces information; the software controlling storage and retrieval is a DBMS; and centralized structured storage is the database itself.

questions.q: Information is best described as which of the following?
o: The result of combining, comparing, and performing calculations on data
A set of instructions that tells hardware what to do
The physical storage location where facts are kept
Facts collected about a single topic before processing
questions.e: Information is produced when data is combined, compared, and calculated upon. Raw uncombined facts remain data, while instructions that tell hardware what to do are software.

questions.q: A school stores figures such as '312 graduates' and '98% of students pass the math exam' in its system, and later produces next year's budget and class averages from them. Which statement correctly maps this scenario?
o: The stored figures are data, and the budget and averages are information
The stored figures are information, and the budget and averages are data
Both the stored figures and the derived outputs are data
Both the stored figures and the derived outputs are information
questions.e: Values that go into the database are data; outputs derived by combining, comparing, and calculating on them (budgets, averages, projections) are information.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the standard definition of a database?
o: It automatically enforces every business rule that an organization follows
It provides facilities for retrieving, adding, modifying, and deleting data when required
It is a centralized and structured set of data stored on a computer system
It provides facilities for transforming retrieved data into useful information
questions.e: A database is centralized structured storage with facilities for retrieval, maintenance, and transformation of data into information. Enforcing every business rule is not part of the definition — not all business rules can be modeled in a database.

questions.q: In a relational database, a row is also known as which of the following?
questions.e: A row equals a record, also called an instance. A column is the field or attribute. A link/association is terminology used by the network model, not the relational model.

questions.q: In relational database terminology, a column is referred to as which of the following?
questions.e: A column is a field, also called an attribute. A record/instance is a row, and a collection of records is a table.

questions.q: An Order Detail table contains ID, DETAILS, and CUSTOMER_ID, while a Customer table contains ID, NAME, and ADDRESS. What makes this pair of tables a relational database?
o: Each table stores methods that operate on its own data
Each table is organized as a tree of parent and child records
The tables are linked to one another by a common attribute
Each table stores its records in plain-text lines
questions.e: A relational database consists of tables linked by a common attribute — here CUSTOMER_ID in Order Detail corresponds to ID in Customer. Plain-text lines describe flat files, trees describe the hierarchical model, and stored methods describe the object-oriented model.

questions.q: Which statement correctly defines a database management system (DBMS)?
o: A collection of records connected to one another through links
The workstation used by end users to submit requests
A centralized and structured set of data stored on a computer system
Software that controls the storage, organization, and retrieval of data
questions.e: A DBMS is the software layer controlling storage, organization, and retrieval. Centralized structured storage is the database itself, the end-user workstation is a client, and records connected through links describe the network model.

questions.q: The elements of a DBMS are which of the following?
o: Conceptual modeling, database design, and database build
Memory and storage management, data dictionary, and query language
questions.e: The three elements of a DBMS are memory and storage management, the data dictionary, and the query language. Hardware/software/operating system and client/server/application are general computing terms, and conceptual modeling, design, and build are the phases of the database development process.

questions.q: Which key computing term is defined as software that directly controls the hardware?
questions.e: The operating system directly controls the hardware. An application performs a specific task, a client is the end-user workstation, and a server accepts work requiring more power from clients.

questions.q: Which term describes a machine that accepts work requiring more power from clients?
questions.e: A server accepts work that requires more processing power than the client can supply. A client is the workstation used by end users, and hardware refers to the physical parts of a computer.

questions.q: The transformations in computing occurred in which chronological order?
questions.e: The order is mainframe computing (1970s), desktop computing (1980s), client/server computing (1990s), grid computing (2000s onward), and cloud computing (2010s).

questions.q: Mainframe computing of the 1970s is characterized as which type of processing?
questions.e: Mainframe computing is centralized processing. Desktop computing is localized, grid computing is shared, and cloud computing is Internet based.

questions.q: Which computing era is described as localized processing?
questions.e: Desktop computing in the 1980s is localized processing, because PCs became fast enough that processing moved from mainframes to the clients themselves.

questions.q: Grid computing is described as which type of processing?
questions.e: Grid computing is shared processing: all of an organization's computers in different locations are used like a pool of computing resources. Internet based processing describes cloud computing.

questions.q: Smaller computers known as 'dumb terminals' were characteristic of which era?
questions.e: Dumb terminals were used in the 1970s to access the mainframe and execute commands. They depended on the mainframe, displayed results only after mainframe processing completed, and were not capable of much processing on their own.

questions.q: As PCs became faster and gained their own software in the 1980s, what were they called?
questions.e: PCs capable of doing some processing on their own became known as smart clients or workstations. Thin clients belong to the 1990s client/server era, where the client mainly runs a GUI interface and browser.

questions.q: Common applications such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint were created during which computing era?
questions.e: Processing power inside the client machine during the desktop era ushered in a wave of graphical user interface applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

questions.q: In the 1990s client/server architecture, how do thin clients reach the essential business applications?
o: By querying the data dictionary directly
By logging directly into the mainframe through a dumb terminal
By installing every business application locally
questions.e: Clients may have their own applications, but the essential business applications are accessed from the clients using an Internet browser. That is why the client tier is described as thin.

questions.q: In a three-tier client/server arrangement, which component performs the processing for document creation, developing, interacting with, or manipulating data?
questions.e: Applications for business operations sit on the application server. The database server holds the software that manages data and performs processing for storage and retrieval.

questions.q: Which cloud service category allows you to rent cloud-based servers, storage, and operating systems?
questions.e: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) rents out servers, storage, and operating systems. PaaS supplies an online environment for developing and testing software, and SaaS delivers finished software over the Internet.

questions.q: A vendor delivers finished software directly over the Internet, and users normally access it through a web browser. Which cloud service category is this?
questions.e: Software as a Service (SaaS) delivers software direct from the Internet, normally accessed through a web browser. IaaS rents infrastructure and PaaS supplies a development and testing environment.

questions.q: Which cloud service category gives access to an online environment for developing and testing software without setup or management costs?
questions.e: Platform as a Service (PaaS) provides the development and testing environment with no setup or management overhead. IaaS supplies raw infrastructure and SaaS supplies finished applications.

questions.q: Who proposed the relational model for databases in 1970-72?
questions.e: E.F. Codd proposed the relational model in 1970-72. P. Chen proposed the entity relationship model in 1976.

questions.q: The relational model proposed in 1970-72 is notable for disconnecting which two things?
o: The logical organization from the physical storage
The data dictionary from the query language
questions.e: The key contribution of the relational model was separating the logical organization of data from its physical storage, so users need not know how data is physically stored.

questions.q: Who proposed the entity relationship model (ERM) for database design, and in what year?
questions.e: P. Chen proposed the entity relationship model in 1976, four to six years after Codd's relational model of 1970-72.

questions.q: The first commercially available relational database systems appeared at the beginning of the 1980s with which product?
questions.e: Oracle Version 2 marked the arrival of commercially available relational database systems in the early 1980s. 10g and 12c are much later releases.

questions.q: Structured Query Language (SQL) became widely used during which period?
questions.e: SQL came into wide use in the mid-1980s, shortly after the first commercial relational systems appeared in the early 1980s.

questions.q: What development in the 1960s helped set the stage for database systems?
o: Computers became cost-effective for private companies, along with increased storage capability
Cloud-based services became a multi-billion dollar industry
questions.e: In the 1960s computers became cost-effective for private companies and storage capability increased. The relational model came in 1970-72, wide SQL use in the mid-1980s, and the cloud boom in the 2010s.

questions.q: What effect did the large investment in Internet companies during the 1990s have on database technology?
o: It turned cloud computing into a multi-billion dollar industry
It introduced the entity relationship model for database design
It created a tools market boom for web, Internet, and database connectors
It produced the first commercially available relational database systems
questions.e: The 1990s investment wave drove a boom in the market for web/Internet/database connector tools. The first commercial relational systems arrived earlier, in the early 1980s, and the cloud industry matured in the 2010s.

questions.q: Which of these are given as typical database applications in the 2000s?
o: Only dumb terminals connected to a central mainframe
Only cloud services rented from Oracle, Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon
Only mainframe payroll systems inside private companies
Commercial websites such as yahoo.com and amazon.com, plus government systems, art museums, hospitals, and schools
questions.e: The 2000s saw solid growth of database applications across commercial websites, government systems such as the Bureau of Citizenship and Immigration Services and the Bureau of the Census, art museums, hospitals, and schools. Cloud services from Oracle, Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon belong to the 2010s.

questions.q: Which industry example matches the use of databases for reservations and for displaying schedule information?
questions.e: Airlines and railways use online databases for reservations and schedule display. Banks store customers, accounts, loans, and transactions; schools store courses, students, and faculty; telecom stores network details, telephone numbers, call details, and monthly bills.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the phases of the database development process?
questions.e: Business information requirements feed strategy and analysis (conceptual data modeling), then design (database design), then build (database build), which finally produces the database.

questions.q: Conceptual data modeling belongs to which phase of the database development process?
questions.e: Conceptual data modeling is the activity of the strategy and analysis phase. The design phase produces the database design and the build phase constructs the database.

questions.q: What forms the starting input to the database development process?
questions.e: Business information requirements drive the whole process, entering at conceptual data modeling and flowing through design and build to the finished database.

questions.q: Which database model is designed around a single table?
questions.e: A flat file database is designed around one single table. Hierarchical and network models connect multiple records through links, and the object-oriented model stores objects belonging to classes.

questions.q: Flat file databases are generally stored in which form?
o: Indexed table form, where each row is addressed by a primary key
Binary tree form, where each node holds one record
Plain-text form, where each line holds only one record
Compiled class form, where each object holds its own methods
questions.e: Flat files are generally plain text with one record per line, and fields within a record are separated by delimiters such as tabs and commas.

questions.q: In a flat file database, how are the fields within a record separated?
o: By delimiters such as tabs and commas
By links between parent and child records
questions.e: Delimiters such as tabs and commas separate the fields inside each record line of a flat file.

questions.q: A single table stores AUTHOR_ID, AUTHOR_NAME, and TITLE, and the author AD0003 (Oliver Goldsmith) appears in two separate rows for two different titles. What weakness does this illustrate?
o: The two rows violate the rule that every table must have a primary key
Storing both books and authors in one table causes repetition of data values
The author record has been split across two linked child records
The author has been modeled as an object with two behaviors
questions.e: Because books and authors are held in a single table, author details repeat once per book. Splitting authors and books into related tables is what removes this repetition.

questions.q: In the hierarchical database model, how is data organized?
o: In a collection of tables linked by common fields
In classes from which objects are instantiated
In a tree-like structure, with records connected through links
questions.e: The hierarchical model organizes data in a tree, storing records that are connected to one another through links. Each record is a collection of fields.

questions.q: A record in the hierarchical database model corresponds to what in the relational database model?
questions.e: A hierarchical record maps to a relational row, since both hold one instance made up of a collection of fields.

questions.q: A membership structure has Members at the top, with Student, Faculty, and Corporate beneath it, and Faculty further divided into Full Time and Part Time. Which model does this represent?
questions.e: A single root branching into children, one of which branches again, is a tree — the defining shape of the hierarchical model. The network model would allow a record to have several parents rather than one.

questions.q: In the network model, what is a link?
o: A method that operates on an object's state
A single data value inside a field
A column shared by two tables
questions.e: A link is an association between two records. In network diagrams boxes represent fields and lines represent links, and each record is a collection of fields containing only one data value each.

questions.q: In a network model diagram, what do boxes and lines represent respectively?
o: Boxes are tables and lines are primary keys
Boxes are fields and lines are links
Boxes are classes and lines are inheritance paths
Boxes are links and lines are fields
questions.e: Boxes stand for fields and lines stand for links, which are the associations between records.

questions.q: In a network database, Oliver Blake is linked to banks BNK001 and BNK005 while Leo Smith is linked to BNK005, BNK007, and BNK009. Which bank record is shared between the two customers?
questions.e: BNK005 is linked to both customers, which shows the flexibility of the network model: one record can be associated with several other records at the same time.

questions.q: The network model is best characterized as which of the following?
o: A flexible way of representing objects and their relationships
A model in which data and methods are encapsulated together
A model built strictly around a single plain-text table
A model in which every child record has exactly one parent
questions.e: The network model is a flexible way of representing objects and their relationships, since records may be connected to multiple other records through links, unlike the strict single-parent tree of the hierarchical model.

questions.q: In the object-oriented model, what is the state of an object?
o: The set of values for the attributes of the object
The class from which the object was derived
The link connecting the object to another object
The set of methods that operate on the object
questions.e: State is the set of attribute values, while behavior is the set of methods that operate on that state.

questions.q: In the object-oriented model, how is the relationship between objects achieved?
o: Through parent-child links in a tree
Through delimiters within a record line
questions.e: Objects relate to one another through sharing of access. Foreign keys belong to the relational model, tree links to the hierarchical model, and delimiters to flat files.

questions.q: Which statement about classes and objects in the object-oriented model is correct?
o: An object must belong to only one class, and a new subclass can be derived from an existing superclass
An object may belong to several classes at once, and subclasses cannot be derived
Objects and classes are the same thing under different names
A class must belong to only one object, and superclasses are derived from subclasses
questions.e: An object is an instance of exactly one class, and a new class (subclass) can be derived from an existing class (superclass).

questions.q: Two Employee items are created from an Employee class, one with id 215 63 2179 and lastName Smith, the other with id 215 63 2180 and lastName John. What does this demonstrate?
o: Two classes derived from a common superclass
Two records linked by a foreign key
Two objects instantiated from the same class, each with its own attribute values
Two rows of a flat file separated by delimiters
questions.e: Both items are objects created from one class; they share the same attribute and method definitions but hold different values for id and lastName.

questions.q: In the relational model, what must be true of the values within any single column?
o: They must be stored in ascending order
They may hold several values in one field where needed
They must all be different from one another
They must come from the same domain, that is the same datatype
questions.e: All values in a column come from the same domain (datatype), and each field holds only one value. Uniqueness is required of rows, not of every column value, and row and column order is not important.

questions.q: Which of the following is a rule of the relational model?
o: A field may contain multiple values if they share a datatype
The order of the rows and columns is not important
Two rows in a table may be exact duplicates
Rows must be physically stored in primary key order
questions.e: Row and column order is insignificant in the relational model. Every row is unique and each field contains only one value.

questions.q: Which naming rule applies to relational tables?
o: Table names must be unique, and column names must be unique within each table
Table names may repeat if the columns differ
Column names must match the table name they belong to
Column names must be unique across the entire database
questions.e: Table names are unique database-wide, but column name uniqueness is only required within a table — so two different tables may both contain a column called ID.

questions.q: An EMPLOYEE table holds EMPLOYEE_ID, FIRST_NAME, LAST_NAME, and DEPARTMENT_ID, and a DEPARTMENT table holds DEPARTMENT_ID and DEPARTMENT_NAME. What role does DEPARTMENT_ID play in each table?
o: It is the primary key of both tables
It is the primary key in EMPLOYEE and the foreign key in DEPARTMENT
It is a unique key in EMPLOYEE and an ordinary column in DEPARTMENT
It is the foreign key in EMPLOYEE and the primary key in DEPARTMENT
questions.e: DEPARTMENT_ID uniquely identifies each department, so it is the primary key of DEPARTMENT; the same column appearing in EMPLOYEE refers back to it, making it a foreign key there and creating the relationship between the tables.

questions.q: Which set of factors creates the need for a database solution?
o: Multiple delimiters, multiple text files, and multiple printers
Multiple programming languages, multiple compilers, and multiple classes
Multiple users, multiple data items, and integration of multiple components
Multiple operating systems, multiple browsers, and multiple servers
questions.e: The need for a database solution arises when many users must share data, when there are many data items to hold, and when multiple components must be integrated.

questions.q: A single table records each student along with SPORT_1, PRICE_1, SPORT_2, and PRICE_2 for the sports they selected. What does this design demonstrate?
o: A flat file with repeating column groups, which warrants a relational database instead
A hierarchical design in which sports are children of students
An object-oriented design in which each sport is a method of the student
A properly normalized relational design with one foreign key per sport
questions.e: Repeating groups of columns for each additional sport is a flat file weakness: a student taking a third sport would need new columns. Splitting the data into related tables is the relational solution.

questions.q: A flat file of students and the sports they selected is split into a Student Details table, a Sport Details table, and a Participant Details table. Which problems does this eliminate?
o: Slow query response, deadlocks, and network latency
Loss of confidentiality, loss of encryption, and loss of backups
Poor indexing, poor sorting, and poor report formatting
Redundancy, data entry anomalies, and inconsistency
questions.e: Splitting the single table into three related tables removes repeated values (redundancy), the anomalies that arise when repeated values are entered, and the resulting inconsistency.

questions.q: Student details and sport details are held in two separate tables. A third table holds STUDENT_ID, SPORT_ID, and SEMESTER_DETAILS. What is the purpose of this third table?
o: To hold the price of each sport so it need not repeat
To act as the data dictionary for the other two tables
To record which student participates in which sport, along with the semester
To store a duplicate copy of the student record for backup
questions.e: The participant table pairs a student with a sport and adds semester information, which is what lets one student take many sports without repeating student or sport details. The price belongs to the sport table.

questions.q: Why are business rules important when designing a database?
o: They let the developer or architect understand the relationships and constraints of the participating entities
They determine which operating system the database will run on
They define the delimiters used to separate fields
They replace the need for a conceptual model
questions.e: Business rules expose entity relationships and constraints, and they reveal the standardization procedures an organization follows when handling large volumes of data.

questions.q: Which pair of qualities should business rules have?
o: Simple and easy to understand, and kept up-to-date
Highly technical and written in SQL
Fixed permanently once written, and known only to the architect
questions.e: Business rules should be simple and easily understood, and they must be kept current as the business changes.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a typical source of business rules?
questions.e: Business rules come from managers, policy makers, documentation and operation manuals, organizational procedures and standards, and interviews with end users. The data dictionary is a DBMS element that describes stored structures, not a source of business policy.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of business rules in relation to data?
o: To measure the retrieval speed of the data
To decide the physical disk layout of the data
To understand business processes and the nature, role, and scope of the data
To define the query language syntax
questions.e: Business rules are used to understand business processes and the nature, role, and scope of the data, which then helps categorize and design the database tables.

questions.q: Which statement about a conceptual model is correct?
o: It is produced after the database has been built
It describes the information needs of the business and forms a sound basis for physical database design
It records only the hardware and operating system requirements
It replaces the physical database design entirely
questions.e: A conceptual model describes the information needs of the business, facilitates discussion, prevents mistakes and misunderstandings, forms 'ideal system' documentation, documents the business rules, accounts for governing regulations and laws, and forms the basis for physical design.

questions.q: Which statement about modeling business rules is correct?
o: Business rules cannot be documented in a conceptual model
Business rules are modeled only after the database is built
Every business rule can be enforced by database constraints
Not all business rules can be modeled in a database
questions.e: Some rules fall outside what a database structure can enforce, so not all business rules can be modeled in a database even though the conceptual model documents them.

questions.q: How is an assumption defined when gathering requirements?
o: A fact or a statement that has been taken for granted
A limit placed on the values an attribute may hold
A statement used to understand business processes and the scope of data
A situation that requires attention and a possible solution
questions.e: An assumption is something taken for granted rather than verified. A problem is a situation needing attention and a solution, and a business rule describes business processes and the nature, role, and scope of data.

questions.q: How is a problem defined when gathering requirements?
o: A fact taken for granted without verification
A situation or scenario that requires attention and a possible solution to alleviate it
A restriction on which values are permitted in a column
A rule that governs the nature, role, and scope of data
questions.e: A problem is a situation needing attention and a remedy, which distinguishes it from an assumption (taken for granted) and a business rule (governs processes and data).

questions.q: A library's requirements notes include: 'To ensure that new book arrivals happen on the 21st of every month.' How should this note be classified?
questions.e: It states a process the organization intends to follow, which makes it a business rule rather than an unverified belief (assumption) or a situation needing remedy (problem).

questions.q: A library's requirements notes include: 'Librarian cannot easily identify DVDs that are seriously overdue (more than two weeks late).' How should this note be classified?
questions.e: It describes a situation requiring attention and a solution, so it is a problem. A business rule would state what the organization does; an assumption would state something taken for granted.

questions.q: A library's requirements notes include: 'Our current system probably uses Oracle Database 10g and is on UNIX.' How should this note be classified?
questions.e: The word 'probably' signals an unverified statement taken for granted, which is an assumption rather than an established rule or an identified problem.

questions.q: An online book rental company plans gold, silver, and bronze memberships, with more types possibly added later. If 'Members will pay membership fees' is treated as the business rule, what is the matching constraint?
o: Members can belong to one of the three types of membership: gold, silver, or bronze
Members must renew their membership every year
Members receive privileges regardless of membership type
Members may hold several memberships simultaneously
questions.e: The rule states that fees are paid; the constraint restricts membership to one of the three defined types. Note that only silver and gold incur a fee, since bronze is free.

questions.q: For an online book rental company, 'Bronze membership is free, while silver and gold memberships incur a fee' is stated as the business rule. What is the accompanying constraint?
o: The type of membership cannot be changed
Only three membership types may ever exist
Bronze members receive the same privileges as gold members
Membership fees must be paid annually
questions.e: The constraint is that a member's type cannot be changed once set. The number of types is not fixed permanently, since additional types may be introduced later.

questions.q: Under a gold, silver, and bronze membership scheme, which memberships entitle the member to privileges in return for a fee?
questions.e: Bronze membership is free. Silver and gold memberships incur a fee but entitle the member to privileges.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of a flat file database?
o: Fast performance on huge data volumes
All records are stored in one place
questions.e: Flat files are easy to understand, easy to implement, easy to extract information from, keep all records in one place, allow simple sorting and filtering of reports, and need less hardware and software. Weak security, redundancy, and poor performance at scale are its disadvantages.

questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of a flat file database?
o: Difficult sorting and filtering of reports
questions.e: Sharing information from a flat file is cumbersome. Simple sorting and filtering, low hardware and software requirements, and easy implementation are listed among its advantages, not its drawbacks.

questions.q: Which group lists only disadvantages of a flat file database?
o: Less security, data inconsistency, data redundancy, slow for huge databases
Slow for huge databases, less hardware requirements, cumbersome sharing
Data inconsistency, data redundancy, easy to understand, simple filtering
Less security, easy to implement, data redundancy, all records in one place
questions.e: The disadvantages are weaker security, data inconsistency, data redundancy, cumbersome information sharing, and slow performance on huge databases. Ease of implementation, single-location storage, simple filtering, and low hardware needs are advantages.

questions.q: In a relational database, what does each column and each row represent?
o: Each column lists one record and each row represents a field
Each column represents a particular type of information (a field) and each row lists one record
Each column represents a table and each row represents a database
Each column stores a delimiter and each row stores a link
questions.e: Columns are fields describing a type of information; rows are records. Tables are then related to one another using a common field.

questions.q: What is used to identify each record uniquely in a relational database?
o: A unique field called a key
The physical row position in storage
The name of the table containing the row
questions.e: A unique field called a key identifies each record. The primary key uniquely identifies each entity instance in its table.

questions.q: A STUDENTS table holds ID, LAST_NAME, DATE_OF_BIRTH, ADDRESS, and COURSE_ID, while a COURSES table holds ID, NAME, and DURATION. What is COURSE_ID in the STUDENTS table?
o: A foreign key referring to the primary key of COURSES
A unique key that prevents two students sharing a course
An ordinary column with no relational significance
questions.e: A primary key column of one table designated in a related table becomes a foreign key there. COURSE_ID points at the COURSES primary key, which is what lets you query the courses a student is attending or has attended.

questions.q: What is the defining function of a primary key column?
o: It records the physical storage address of the row
It refers to a column in another table
It uniquely identifies each entity instance in its table
It stores the same value in every row of the table
questions.e: A primary key uniquely identifies each instance (row). A column that refers to another table's primary key is a foreign key.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of a relational (multiple-table) database rather than a flat file?
o: All records stored in one place
questions.e: Relational databases offer less redundancy, avoidance of inconsistency, efficiency, data integrity, and confidentiality. Keeping all records in one place, low hardware needs, and easy implementation are flat file advantages.

questions.q: Which list contains only advantages of a relational (multiple-table) database?
o: Less redundancy, avoidance of inconsistency, efficiency, data integrity, confidentiality
Less redundancy, easy implementation, all records in one place, confidentiality
Efficiency, confidentiality, plain-text storage, single-table design
Data integrity, less security, efficiency, avoidance of inconsistency
questions.e: The five advantages of the multiple-table approach are less redundancy, avoidance of inconsistency, efficiency, data integrity, and confidentiality.

questions.q: An EMPLOYEES table contains EMPLOYEE_ID, LAST_NAME, FIRST_NAME, DEPARTMENT_ID, PAYROLL_ID, and NICKNAME. EMPLOYEE_ID is the primary key and DEPARTMENT_ID is the foreign key. Which column serves as the unique key?
questions.e: PAYROLL_ID holds a distinct value per employee without being the table's primary key, which makes it a unique key. Nicknames and names are not guaranteed distinct.

questions.q: Which of these is a rule for relational database tables?
o: Two tables may share the same name if their columns differ
Entries in columns are single values
Rows must be kept in a fixed order
Entries in a column may mix different kinds of data
questions.e: Each column entry holds a single value, all entries in a column are of the same kind, row and column order is insignificant, and each table has a distinct name.

questions.q: Which statement about ordering in a relational table is correct?
o: The order of rows and columns is insignificant
Rows must be ordered by primary key but columns may vary
Columns must be ordered with the primary key first
Both rows and columns must be stored in alphabetical order
questions.e: Order of rows and columns carries no meaning in the relational model; data is located by key values and column names, not by position.

questions.q: Which naming requirements apply to relational database tables?
o: Each table has a distinct name and each column in a table has a unique name
Column names must be unique across all tables in the database
Table names must include the name of their primary key
Each table has a distinct name but columns may repeat within a table
questions.e: Table names must be distinct, and within any one table each column name must be unique. Uniqueness of column names is not required across different tables.

questions.q: Which term describes the one value found at the intersection of a row and a column?
questions.e: A field is the single value where a row and a column meet. A row is the data for one table instance and a column is an attribute describing information in the table.

questions.q: Which term is defined as the data for one table instance?
questions.e: A row holds the data for one instance of the table. A field is a single value at a row-column intersection, and a column is an attribute of the table.

questions.q: Which term is defined as the attribute that describes the information in a table?
questions.e: A column is the attribute describing what kind of information the table holds. A foreign key is a specific kind of column that refers to another table's primary key.

questions.q: Which term is defined as the basic storage structure of a relational database?
questions.e: A table is the basic storage structure — a simple structure where data is organized and stored in rows and columns.

questions.q: Which definition matches a foreign key?
o: A column whose values may never repeat anywhere in the database
A column that refers to a primary key column in another table
The one value found at the intersection of a row and column
The unique identifier for each row of its own table
questions.e: A foreign key refers to a primary key column in another table, forming the relationship between them. The unique identifier of a row within its own table is the primary key.

questions.q: A single table lists AUTHOR_ID, AUTHOR_NAME, and TITLE, and one author's ID and name appear twice because that author wrote two books. Which flat file disadvantage does this show?
questions.e: The repeated author ID and name in multiple rows is data redundancy, which in turn leads to data inconsistency if one copy is later updated and another is not.

questions.q: Which type of data model captures the functional and informational needs of a business but deliberately says nothing about how those needs will be implemented?
questions.e: A conceptual model addresses what is conceptually ideal for the business, not what is physically possible. The logical model adds attributes, UIDs, optionality and cardinality; the physical model handles implementation in a specific database.

questions.q: A conceptual data model identifies which two things?
o: Important entities and the relationships among them
Views, indexes, and other database objects
questions.e: The conceptual model documents important entities and how they relate to each other. Attributes and unique identifiers are deliberately left out at this stage; data types and database objects belong to the physical model.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT specified in a conceptual data model?
o: The informational needs of the business
questions.e: A conceptual model does not specify attributes or unique identifiers. It stops at entities, their relationships, and the business needs those represent.

questions.q: Entities identified during conceptual modelling eventually become which object in the finished database?
questions.e: Entities map to tables. Attributes map to columns or fields, the unique identifier maps to the primary key, and relationships map to foreign keys.

questions.q: When a data model is implemented, attributes become which database object?
questions.e: Attributes become the columns (fields) of a table. Entities become the tables themselves and relationships become foreign keys.

questions.q: When a data model is implemented, a unique identifier becomes which database object?
questions.e: The unique identifier of an entity becomes the primary key of the corresponding table. Foreign keys come from relationships, not from unique identifiers.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the time horizon of a conceptual data model?
o: It is based only on needs that already exist and cannot anticipate anything else
It is based on current needs but may also reflect future needs
It is based only on projected future needs
It is fixed at the moment of implementation and is never revised
questions.e: A conceptual model is grounded in current business needs, but it may also reflect future needs. It is not restricted to either the present or the future alone.

questions.q: A logical data model is also known by which other name?
questions.e: The logical model is called an entity relationship model (ERM), and it is drawn out as an entity relationship diagram (ERD).

questions.q: A logical data model is illustrated using which diagram?
questions.e: The logical model, or entity relationship model, is illustrated in an ERD. A relationship matrix is only a tool for collecting initial information about relationships, not the model diagram itself.

questions.q: Which of the following is determined by the logical data model but is absent from the conceptual data model?
o: How objects are implemented in a specific database
questions.e: The logical model specifies all attributes and UIDs for each entity, determines attribute optionality, and determines relationship optionality and cardinality. Entities already exist at the conceptual stage; implementation details and data types belong to the physical model.

questions.q: Which data model defines table definitions, data types, and precision?
questions.e: Defining table definitions, data types, and precision is the job of the physical data model. It also identifies views, indexes, and other database objects.

questions.q: Identifying views, indexes, and other database objects is a characteristic of which data model?
questions.e: Views, indexes, and other database objects appear only in the physical model, which describes how objects should be implemented in a specific database.

questions.q: The physical data model is best described as an extension of which model?
questions.e: The physical data model is an extension of the logical data model, adding table definitions, data types, precision, and other database objects on top of the entities, attributes, and relationships already defined.

questions.q: Which model shows all table structures, including columns, primary keys, and foreign keys?
questions.e: Showing complete table structures with columns, primary keys, and foreign keys is a property of the physical model. The logical model shows entities, attributes, and UIDs but not implemented table structures.

questions.q: What is the FIRST step in creating a physical data model?
o: Modify the model based on physical constraints and requirements
questions.e: The order is: model entities as tables, then model relationships as foreign keys, then model attributes as columns, and finally modify the physical model based on physical constraints and requirements.

questions.q: In building a physical data model, which step comes immediately after modelling relationships as foreign keys?
o: Modifying the model for physical constraints
questions.e: The sequence runs entities to tables, relationships to foreign keys, attributes to columns, and then modification for physical constraints and requirements. So modelling attributes as columns follows the foreign key step.

questions.q: What is the LAST step in creating a physical data model?
o: Modifying the physical data model based on physical constraints and requirements
Naming both perspectives of each relationship
questions.e: After entities, relationships, and attributes have been converted into tables, foreign keys, and columns, the final step is to modify the physical model to account for physical constraints and requirements.

questions.q: Data modelling is best defined as which of the following?
o: Writing the SQL statements that create tables and constraints
Capturing the important concepts and rules that shape a business and depicting them visually in a diagram
Loading business data into a set of normalized tables
Measuring the storage and performance requirements of a database
questions.e: Data modelling captures a business's important concepts and rules and depicts them visually in a diagram, and that diagram then becomes the blueprint for designing the physical thing.

questions.q: In the analogy that a client's dream becomes a physical reality, the client's dream corresponds to which model?
questions.e: The conceptual model represents the client's dream, and the physical model represents that dream turned into physical reality.

questions.q: A simplified library database is built with the entities MEMBER, BOOK, AUTHOR, and PUBLISHER. When this design is converted into a physical model, the relationships between these entities become which objects?
questions.e: In the conversion to a physical model, entities become tables, attributes become columns, and relationships become foreign keys.

questions.q: In a simplified library database, each book may be written by several authors and each author may write several books. In the physical model this is implemented as a BOOK_AUTHORS table whose primary key is made up of BOOKS_Id and AUTHORS_Id together. What kind of primary key is this?
questions.e: A primary key built from more than one column, such as BOOKS_Id plus AUTHORS_Id, is a composite primary key. Both columns are simultaneously foreign keys pointing back to the BOOKS and AUTHORS tables.

questions.q: In a simplified library data model, a MEMBER entity records First name, Last name, Street Address, City, State, and ZIP, and State is the only one of these marked with a lowercase o. What does that tell you about State?
o: It is the unique identifier of MEMBER
It is an optional attribute that may be left null
It is a foreign key to another entity
questions.e: A lowercase o marks an optional attribute, meaning nulls are allowed. An asterisk would mark a mandatory attribute and a hash mark would indicate the unique identifier.

questions.q: In a physical library model, the BOOKS table has a primary key on Id and a separate unique key constraint on Title. What does the unique key on Title enforce?
o: That every book must have at least one author
That no two rows may store the same book title
That Title may be left null for some books
That Title is a foreign key to the PUBLISHERS table
questions.e: A unique key constraint guarantees that values in that column are not duplicated across rows, so no two books could share a title. It is separate from the primary key, which is defined on Id.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct description of an entity?
o: Information that must be tracked, named for things you can list, usually in noun form
A single-valued property detail that describes something
A bidirectional association between two things
A value that uniquely identifies a single occurrence
questions.e: An entity is information that must be tracked and is a name for things that you can list, usually expressed as a noun. A single-valued property detail is an attribute, an association is a relationship, and a uniquely identifying value is a unique identifier.

questions.q: A district hotel manager wants to manage information about her company's hotels, guests, and rooms across several locations, including what rooms exist in each hotel, the price of each room, and which rooms have been reserved for a particular date by a guest. Which of the following is an entity in this situation rather than an attribute?
questions.e: The entities here are GUEST, HOTEL, ROOM, and RESERVATION. Price, date, and location are details that describe those entities, so they behave as attributes rather than entities.

questions.q: An entity that exists independently of any other entity is classified as which type?
questions.e: A prime entity exists independently; CUSTOMER and INSTRUCTOR are examples. A characteristic entity exists because of another prime entity, and an intersection entity exists because of two or more entities.

questions.q: An entity that exists only because of another prime entity is classified as which type?
questions.e: A characteristic entity exists because of another (prime) entity; ORDER and CLASS OFFERING are examples. Intersection entities differ in that they exist because of two or more entities.

questions.q: An entity that exists because of two or more other entities is classified as which type?
questions.e: An intersection entity exists because of two or more entities; ORDER ITEM and CLASS ENROLLMENT are examples. A characteristic entity depends on only one prime entity.

questions.q: CLASS ENROLLMENT is an example of which type of entity?
questions.e: CLASS ENROLLMENT, like ORDER ITEM, exists because of two or more entities, making it an intersection entity. CLASS OFFERING, by contrast, is a characteristic entity.

questions.q: ORDER and CLASS OFFERING are given as examples of which entity type?
questions.e: ORDER and CLASS OFFERING each exist because of another prime entity, which makes them characteristic entities. ORDER ITEM and CLASS ENROLLMENT are the corresponding intersection examples.

questions.q: What is an entity instance?
o: A single occurrence of an entity
A property detail that describes an entity
A group of entities related by a foreign key
The name given to a relationship perspective
questions.e: An entity instance is a single occurrence of an entity. Entities contain instances and represent the set of instances that interest a particular business.

questions.q: If 'Nail' is an instance of the entity PRODUCT TYPE, which entity does '2.5 x 35 mm copper nail' most appropriately serve as an instance of?
questions.e: The general classification 'Nail' is an instance of PRODUCT TYPE, whereas the specific item '2.5 x 35 mm copper nail' is an instance of PRODUCT.

questions.q: 'Violinist' is best described as an instance of which entity?
questions.e: Violinist is one occurrence of the entity JOB, alongside instances such as clerk, accountant, manager, teacher, waitress, and financial controller. John Smith would be an instance of PERSON.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes an attribute?
o: A name for a thing that you can list
A single-valued property detail that describes an entity and must be known
A bidirectional association between two entities
A rule that determines how many instances participate in a relationship
questions.e: Attributes describe entities and are the specific information that must be known; an attribute is a single-valued property detail of an entity. Note that the same material later introduces multi-valued attributes, which sits awkwardly with the word 'single-valued' in this definition.

questions.q: How should attribute names be written?
o: Singular and mixed case or lowercase
questions.e: Attribute names are singular and written in mixed case or lowercase. Fully uppercase, singular names are the convention for entity names, not attribute names.

questions.q: Why should an attribute's name normally avoid repeating the name of its entity?
o: Because attributes are already qualified with the entity name
Because attribute names must be a single word
Because the entity name is stored separately as a foreign key
Because repeating it would make the attribute mandatory
questions.e: Attributes are qualified with the entity name, so including the entity name inside the attribute name is redundant.

questions.q: In Barker notation, which symbol placed next to an attribute indicates that it is mandatory?
questions.e: An asterisk marks a mandatory attribute, a lowercase o marks an optional attribute, and a hash sign marks the unique identifier. A capital P is the Bachman notation symbol for a primary key.

questions.q: An attribute is marked with a lowercase o. What does this indicate?
o: It is the entity's unique identifier
It must always have a value
Nulls are allowed, so it may be left blank
questions.e: A lowercase o indicates an optional attribute, meaning nulls are allowed and the attribute may not have a value. Mandatory attributes, marked with an asterisk, must have a value.

questions.q: Which pair correctly matches an attribute with its volatility?
o: Age is nonvolatile; Date of Birth is volatile
Age is volatile; Date of Birth is nonvolatile
Both Age and Date of Birth are volatile
Both Age and Date of Birth are nonvolatile
questions.e: Volatile attributes are unstable and Age is the standard example, since it changes every year. Nonvolatile attributes are stable, and Date of Birth never changes.

questions.q: Nonvolatile attributes are best described as which of the following?
o: Attributes with more than one value at a time
questions.e: Nonvolatile attributes are stable, such as Birth Date. Volatile attributes are unstable, such as Age. Nullability and multi-valuedness are separate classifications.

questions.q: An attribute that can be divided into smaller subparts, each with an independent meaning of its own, is called what?
questions.e: A composite attribute can be broken into smaller basic attributes with independent meanings, such as Name splitting into First Name, Middle Name, and Last Name. An atomic (single) attribute cannot be divided.

questions.q: An EMPLOYEE entity holds Name, which can be broken into First Name, Middle Name, and Last Name, and also holds ID, which cannot be broken down further. How are these two attributes classified?
o: Name is single (atomic) and ID is composite
Name is composite and ID is single (atomic)
questions.e: Name divides into meaningful subparts, so it is composite. ID cannot be divided into subparts, so it is a single or atomic attribute.

questions.q: Which of the following is given as the example of a multi-valued attribute?
questions.e: Address is the example of a multi-valued attribute, since it can hold more than one value at one time. Student Last Name is the contrasting example of a single-valued attribute.

questions.q: A single-valued attribute is defined as one that does which of the following?
o: Holds a single value at a particular instance of time
Never changes over the lifetime of the instance
questions.e: A single-valued attribute can have one value at a particular instance of time, such as a student's last name. Being indivisible describes an atomic attribute, and being unchanging describes a nonvolatile attribute.

questions.q: In Barker notation, how is an entity drawn?
questions.e: Barker notation draws an entity as a round-cornered rectangle. Bachman and Information Engineering notations both use plain square-cornered boxes.

questions.q: According to Barker notation rules, where is an entity's name placed and in what form?
o: Centred inside the box, in singular lowercase
Inside the box in the upper-left corner, in uppercase and singular form
Above the box, in uppercase and plural form
Inside the box in the lower-left corner, in mixed case
questions.e: Barker notation requires the entity name to sit inside the entity in the upper-left corner, written in uppercase and in singular form.

questions.q: Under Barker notation rules for drawing relationships, what is the maximum number of entities a single relationship can connect?
questions.e: A relationship can exist between a maximum of two entities, though it may also exist on the same entity, which is a recursive relationship.

questions.q: Barker notation requires which of the following about the two perspectives of a relationship?
o: Only the perspective from the mandatory side must be labelled
Neither perspective is labelled on the diagram
Perspectives are labelled only for recursive relationships
questions.e: A relationship has two perspectives and both must be labelled. Relationships may also be recursive, existing between an entity and itself.

questions.q: Which symbol marks the primary or unique key in Bachman notation?
questions.e: Bachman notation uses a capital P for the primary or unique key, whereas Barker notation uses a hash sign. Information Engineering notation has no dedicated symbol shown for it.

questions.q: Which notation uses a hash sign (#) to mark the primary or unique key?
o: All three use the hash sign
questions.e: Barker notation marks the primary or unique key with a hash sign. Bachman notation uses a capital P instead, and Information Engineering notation shows no symbol for this.

questions.q: In Information Engineering notation, which combination of relationship line symbols represents 'one or more'?
o: A circle and a crow's foot
A bar and a crow's foot
questions.e: A bar with a crow's foot means one or more. A circle with a crow's foot means zero or more, a circle with a bar means zero or one, and two bars mean only one.

questions.q: In Information Engineering notation, which combination of relationship line symbols represents 'zero or more'?
o: A bar and a crow's foot
A circle and a crow's foot
questions.e: A circle combined with a crow's foot means zero or more. The circle contributes the possibility of zero and the crow's foot contributes 'many'.

questions.q: An Information Engineering diagram links EMPLOYEE and DEPARTMENT so that the EMPLOYEE end carries a circle and a crow's foot and the DEPARTMENT end carries two bars. How is this read?
o: An EMPLOYEE works in zero or more DEPARTMENTs, and a DEPARTMENT contains only one EMPLOYEE
An EMPLOYEE works only in one DEPARTMENT, and a DEPARTMENT contains zero or more EMPLOYEEs
An EMPLOYEE works in one or more DEPARTMENTs, and a DEPARTMENT contains one or more EMPLOYEEs
An EMPLOYEE works in zero or one DEPARTMENT, and a DEPARTMENT contains only one EMPLOYEE
questions.e: Two bars at the DEPARTMENT end mean only one, so an employee works in exactly one department. The circle plus crow's foot at the EMPLOYEE end means zero or more, so a department may contain any number of employees, including none.

questions.q: Which three components make up Bachman notation?
o: Entities drawn as boxes, attributes, and relationship lines
Entities drawn as round-cornered rectangles, cardinality symbols, and a relationship matrix
Crow's feet, single toes, and dashed lines
questions.e: Bachman notation consists of an entity represented by a box, its attributes, and relationship lines. Round-cornered rectangles belong to Barker notation, and tables with columns and foreign keys belong to the physical model.

questions.q: Which set of rules must an attribute satisfy to serve as a unique identifier of an entity?
o: It is unique across all instances, has a non-NULL value for the lifetime of each instance, and never changes for the lifetime of the instance
It is unique across all instances, may be null, and is generated by the system
It is mandatory, indivisible, and volatile
It is unique within a single instance, non-NULL, and always numeric
questions.e: A unique identifier must be unique across all instances, must hold a non-NULL value for each instance throughout that instance's lifetime, and must never change during that lifetime. There is no requirement that it be numeric or system generated.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for an attribute to act as a unique identifier?
o: It must be unique across all instances of the entity
It must be non-NULL for the lifetime of the instance
Its value must never change for the lifetime of the instance
It must be generated automatically by the system
questions.e: Uniqueness, non-nullity, and immutability are the three rules. System generation describes an artificial unique identifier, which is only one way of obtaining a UID, not a requirement of all UIDs.

questions.q: A unique identifier is best described as which of the following?
o: A relationship between an entity and itself
A special attribute or group of attributes that uniquely identifies a particular instance of an entity
A column that refers to a primary key in another table
An attribute whose value changes over time
questions.e: A UID is a special attribute, or group of attributes, that uniquely identifies a particular instance of an entity. A column referring to another table's primary key is a foreign key.

questions.q: A candidate thing being modelled has no attribute or combination of attributes that can uniquely identify its occurrences. What follows?
o: It is still an entity, but it needs a foreign key
It becomes an intersection entity automatically
It can only be modelled as an attribute of a relationship
questions.e: Every entity must have a unique identifier; otherwise it is not an entity. If no natural UID exists, an artificial UID can be created so that it qualifies.

questions.q: A DEPARTMENT entity is modelled with a system-assigned ID as its unique identifier plus a Name attribute. How is this unique identifier classified?
questions.e: A single ID attribute is a single-attribute identifier, and because a bare assigned number carries no business meaning it is non-information bearing. A CONCERT TICKET identified by Performance Date plus Seat Number is the contrasting multiple-attribute, information-bearing case.

questions.q: A CONCERT TICKET entity is uniquely identified by the combination of Performance Date and Seat Number. How is this unique identifier classified?
questions.e: Two attributes are needed, making it a multiple-attribute identifier, and both attributes carry real business meaning, making it information bearing.

questions.q: What is a simple unique identifier?
o: A unique identifier made up of a single attribute
A unique identifier made up of a combination of attributes
A unique identifier generated by the system
A unique identifier that is not chosen as the primary UID
questions.e: A UID consisting of one attribute is a simple UID. A UID built from a combination of attributes is a composite UID, and a UID not chosen as primary is a secondary UID.

questions.q: When a single attribute is not enough to uniquely identify an instance and several attributes must be combined, the result is called what?
questions.e: A UID that is a combination of attributes is a composite UID, such as Performance Date plus Seat Number for a concert ticket. An artificial UID is defined by its origin, not by how many attributes it spans.

questions.q: What is an artificial unique identifier?
o: A UID formed by combining two natural attributes
A UID made from data that is assigned or generated by the system
A UID that has been rejected in favour of another candidate
A UID that carries business meaning
questions.e: An artificial UID is made from data assigned or generated by the system. Such identifiers do not occur in the natural world and are created purely for identification purposes within a system.

questions.q: Which statement about artificial unique identifiers is correct?
o: They occur naturally in the business world and are simply recorded
They do not occur in the natural world and are created for identification purposes in a system
They must always be composed of at least two attributes
They may contain null values as long as they are unique
questions.e: Artificial UIDs do not occur in the natural world; they are created for identification purposes within a system from data the system assigns or generates. No UID may be null.

questions.q: A SHOE entity is described only by Color, Size, and Style, none of which can distinguish one shoe from another. What is the standard remedy?
o: Combine Color, Size, and Style into a composite UID
Create an artificial UID such as an ID attribute
Remove Style so the remaining attributes become unique
questions.e: When no natural attribute or combination uniquely identifies instances, an artificial UID such as an ID is created and added to the entity, leaving Color, Size, and Style as ordinary attributes.

questions.q: A MEMBER entity holds First Name, Last Name, and Street Address. Under what condition could First Name combined with Last Name serve as the unique identifier?
o: Only if you are certain that the combination is unique for every member
Always, because two attributes together are automatically unique
Only if Street Address is also included
Never, because names are volatile attributes
questions.e: A combination of first and last name can be used only if you are sure the combination is unique. Because names can repeat across members, the safer solution is to create an artificial UID such as ID.

questions.q: An EMPLOYEE entity could be uniquely identified by either its badge number or its payroll number. What are these two attributes called?
questions.e: When an entity has more than one attribute capable of uniquely identifying it, each is a candidate UID. Only one candidate can be chosen as the primary UID; the rest become secondary UIDs.

questions.q: An entity has three candidate unique identifiers. How many of them may be chosen as the primary UID?
o: None, a new artificial UID must be created
questions.e: Only one of the candidate UIDs can be chosen as the primary UID. The remaining candidates are then referred to as secondary UIDs.

questions.q: Candidate unique identifiers that are not selected as the primary UID are known as what?
questions.e: The candidates left over after the primary UID is chosen are called secondary UIDs. They still uniquely identify instances but are not the designated primary identifier.

questions.q: A MEMBER entity has ID chosen as its primary UID and also stores Email, First Name, Last Name, and Street Address. Which attribute is the candidate UID and why?
o: Street Address, because addresses are recorded in full
Last Name, because it is mandatory
Email, because it is unique for every member
First Name, because it is the first attribute listed
questions.e: Email qualifies as a candidate UID because it is unique for every member. Names and street addresses can be shared by more than one member, so they cannot uniquely identify an instance.

questions.q: At what point does a unique identifier become a primary key?
o: When the conceptual model is drawn
When the logical model is transformed into a physical database
When a second candidate UID is discovered
When the attribute is marked mandatory
questions.e: A UID becomes a primary key when the logical model is transformed into a physical database, which is also the point at which entities become tables and relationships become foreign keys.

questions.q: Which statement about a primary key is correct?
o: It may contain null values as long as the non-null values are unique
It is a column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row and cannot contain null values
It must always be a single column
It always refers to a primary key in another table
questions.e: A primary key is a column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a table, it cannot contain null values, and it must hold a unique value for every row. A column referring to another table's primary key is a foreign key.

questions.q: A primary key column can come from which of the following sources?
o: Only from a column generated by the database according to a defined sequence
Only from an existing business column already in the table
Either an existing table column or a column generated by the database according to a defined sequence
Only from a combination of at least two existing columns
questions.e: A primary key is either an existing table column or a column specifically generated by the database according to a defined sequence. Both single-column and composite primary keys are permitted.

questions.q: An EMPLOYEES table stores EMPLOYEE_ID, FIRST_NAME, LAST_NAME, and DEPARTMENT_ID, with values such as 100 Steven King in department 90 and 205 Shelly Higgins in department 10. EMPLOYEE_ID is the key. What kind of primary key is this?
questions.e: EMPLOYEE_ID alone identifies each row, making it a single-column primary key. DEPARTMENT_ID in the same table points to another table and therefore behaves as a foreign key, not a primary key.

questions.q: An ACCOUNTS table holds BANK_NO, ACCT_NO, BALANCE, and DATE_OPENED, and contains rows for bank 104 with accounts 71432 and 34578, and bank 105 with accounts 78967 and 72345. BANK_NO and ACCT_NO together form the key. What is this arrangement called?
questions.e: Fields combined to form one key make a composite primary key, that is, a primary key consisting of multiple fields. BANK_NO alone repeats across rows, so it could not identify a row on its own.

questions.q: In an ACCOUNTS table holding BANK_NO, ACCT_NO, BALANCE, and DATE_OPENED, one account has a balance of 20,000 but no value recorded in DATE_OPENED. Why does this alone disqualify DATE_OPENED from being part of the primary key?
o: Because a primary key cannot contain null values
Because the balance is not unique
Because a primary key can only contain numeric columns
questions.e: A primary key cannot contain null values, so a column with a missing value in even one row cannot participate in it. This mirrors the UID rule that the identifying value must be non-NULL for the lifetime of every instance.

questions.q: How is a relationship defined?
o: A one-way link from a parent entity to a child entity
A bidirectional, significant association between two entities or between an entity and itself
A column that repeats a value found in another table
A rule stating how many attributes an entity may hold
questions.e: A relationship is a bidirectional, significant association between two entities or between an entity and itself. Because it is bidirectional it has two perspectives, and both are named.

questions.q: On an entity relationship diagram, what does a dashed relationship line indicate?
o: That the relationship connects more than two entities
questions.e: A dashed relationship line indicates that the relationship is optional, while a solid line indicates that it is mandatory.

questions.q: A relationship line terminates in a crow's foot at one end. What does this signify at that end?
questions.e: A crow's foot means one or more instances, while a single toe means one instance. Whether the relationship is mandatory or optional is shown separately, by a solid or dashed line.

questions.q: On a relationship line, what does a 'single toe' termination represent?
questions.e: A single toe represents one instance and a crow's foot represents one or more instances. Optionality is conveyed by whether the line is dashed or solid, not by its termination.

questions.q: Where is a relationship's name printed on a diagram?
o: In the middle of the relationship line, in uppercase
Near the starting point of the relationship line, close to the entity that perspective is assigned to
Inside the entity box that owns the relationship
Only in the relationship matrix, never on the diagram
questions.e: The name of the relationship, from either perspective, is printed near the starting point of the relationship line, that is, close to the entity that name is assigned to. Relationship names are written in lowercase.

questions.q: How should relationship names be written on an entity relationship diagram?
questions.e: All relationship names should be in lowercase, such as 'contain' and 'assigned to'. Entity names, by contrast, are written in uppercase.

questions.q: How is a foreign key defined?
o: A column or combination of columns in one table that refers to a primary key in the same table or another table
A column that uniquely identifies each row in its own table
An attribute assigned or generated by the system
A column that cannot contain null values
questions.e: A foreign key is a column or combination of columns in one table that refers to a primary key in the same table or another table. Uniquely identifying each row in its own table describes a primary key.

questions.q: When a conceptual data model is turned into a physical database, relationships are mapped to which object?
questions.e: Relationships in a conceptual data model are mapped to foreign keys in physical database tables. Unique identifiers become primary keys, and entities become tables.

questions.q: An EMPLOYEES table has columns EMPLOYEE_ID, FIRST_NAME, LAST_NAME, and DEPARTMENT_ID, and a separate DEPARTMENTS table has DEPARTMENT_ID as its primary key with DEPARTMENT_NAME beside it. What role does DEPARTMENT_ID play in the EMPLOYEES table?
o: It is the primary key of EMPLOYEES
It is a foreign key referring to the primary key of DEPARTMENTS
It is a secondary unique identifier of EMPLOYEES
It is a composite key together with EMPLOYEE_ID
questions.e: DEPARTMENT_ID in EMPLOYEES refers to the primary key of DEPARTMENTS, so it is a foreign key. EMPLOYEE_ID remains the primary key of the EMPLOYEES table.

questions.q: Which three components make up a relationship?
o: Name, primary key, and foreign key
questions.e: A relationship consists of a name, its cardinality, and its optionality. Primary and foreign keys are physical implementations, and volatility and precision belong to attributes and columns respectively.

questions.q: Cardinality in a relationship refers to which of the following?
o: The minimum and maximum number of values in the relationship
The direction in which the relationship is read
Whether the related attribute may be null
questions.e: Cardinality measures quantity: the minimum and maximum number of values in the relationship, answering the question 'how many?'. Whether the relationship must exist at all is optionality.

questions.q: Optionality in a relationship answers which question?
o: Which entity owns the foreign key?
questions.e: Optionality determines whether the relationship must exist. Optional means zero matching records are acceptable; mandatory means there must be at least one matching record in each entity.

questions.q: A mandatory relationship is characterised by which of the following?
o: There must be at least one matching record in each entity
Exactly one matching record is permitted
Matching records may be added later
questions.e: Mandatory means at least one matching record must exist in each entity, and it is drawn as a solid line. Optional, drawn as a dashed line, permits zero matching records.

questions.q: When writing a business rule sentence, which wording is used for an optional relationship?
questions.e: Optional relationships are read with 'may be' or 'may', while mandatory relationships use 'must be' or 'must'. The phrases 'one and only one' and 'one or more' express cardinality, coming from a plain line and a crow's foot respectively.

questions.q: In a business rule sentence, which phrase corresponds to a crow's foot on the relationship line?
questions.e: Crow's feet are read as 'one or more', and a plain line ending is read as 'one and only one'. The phrases 'may be' and 'must be' express optionality rather than cardinality.

questions.q: Which of the following gives the correct order of elements in a business rule sentence?
o: Each entity1, then must be or may be, then the relationship name, then one or more or one and only one, then entity2
Each entity1, then the relationship name, then must be or may be, then entity2
The relationship name, then entity1, then entity2, then the cardinality
Each entity1, then one or more or one and only one, then must be or may be, then entity2
questions.e: The syntax runs: Each entity1 {must be or may be} relationship name {one or more or one and only one} entity2. For example, each customer must be visited by one and only one sales representative.

questions.q: What does a minimum cardinality of zero in one direction of a relationship indicate?
o: That the relationship is optional in that direction
That the relationship is mandatory in that direction
That only one instance may participate
questions.e: A minimum cardinality of zero means the relationship is optional in that direction, drawn as a dashed line. A minimum of one means it is mandatory, drawn as a solid line.

questions.q: What does a maximum cardinality of many in one direction of a relationship indicate?
o: One and only one instance may participate
One or more instances may participate
questions.e: A maximum cardinality of many means one or more, shown by a crow's foot. A maximum of one means one and only one, shown by a plain line ending.

questions.q: Many-to-one and one-to-many relationships have which cardinality pattern?
o: One or more in both directions
One and only one in both directions
One or more in one direction and one and only one in the other
Zero or more in one direction and zero in the other
questions.e: M:1 and 1:M relationships have a cardinality of one or more in one direction and one and only one in the other. One or more in both directions is many-to-many, and one and only one in both directions is one-to-one.

questions.q: Many-to-many relationships have which cardinality pattern?
o: One or more in both directions
One and only one in both directions
One or more in one direction and one and only one in the other
Zero in one direction and many in the other
questions.e: A many-to-many relationship has a cardinality of one or more in both directions, so both ends carry a crow's foot.

questions.q: One-to-one relationships have which cardinality pattern?
o: One or more in both directions
One and only one in both directions
One or more in one direction and one and only one in the other
One and only one in one direction and zero in the other
questions.e: A one-to-one relationship has a cardinality of one and only one in both directions, so neither end carries a crow's foot.

questions.q: Two business rules state that each customer must be visited by one and only one sales representative, and each sales representative may be assigned to one or more customers. What type of relationship is this?
questions.e: One direction is 'one and only one' and the other is 'one or more', which is the defining pattern of an M:1 and 1:M relationship. Note also that the customer side is mandatory ('must be') while the sales representative side is optional ('may be').

questions.q: Two business rules state that each employee may be assigned to one or more jobs, and each job may be carried out by one or more employees. What type of relationship is this?
questions.e: Because the cardinality is 'one or more' in both directions, this is a many-to-many relationship. Both perspectives also use 'may', so the relationship is optional in both directions.

questions.q: Two business rules state that each computer must contain one and only one motherboard, and each motherboard must be contained in one and only one computer. What type of relationship is this?
questions.e: Cardinality of one and only one in both directions makes this a one-to-one relationship, and 'must' on both sides makes it mandatory in both directions.

questions.q: What is a recursive relationship?
o: A relationship connecting three or more entities
A relationship with an entity and itself
A relationship whose foreign key is also a primary key
A relationship that is optional in both directions
questions.e: A recursive relationship exists between an entity and itself, such as an employee who manages other employees. A relationship can connect at most two entities.

questions.q: An EMPLOYEE entity carries a relationship to itself in which each employee may manage one or more employees and each employee must be managed by one and only one employee. Which end of this relationship is mandatory?
