o: The 'managed by' perspective, because it uses 'must'
Both perspectives, because it is recursive
Neither, because recursive relationships are always optional
questions.e: 'Must be managed by one and only one employee' is the mandatory perspective and is drawn as a solid line, while 'may manage one or more' is optional and is drawn dashed.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a relationship matrix?
o: To collect initial information about the relationships among a set of entities
To store the foreign key values of a physical database
To record the data types and precision of each column
To list every instance of an entity
questions.e: A relationship matrix is used to collect initial information about the relationships among a set of entities, and its contents can then be mapped to an ERD.

questions.q: In a relationship matrix, what does an empty intersection box mean?
o: The relationship exists but has not yet been named
The row entity is not related to the column entity
questions.e: An empty intersection box means the row entity is not related to the column entity. When a relationship does exist, the name of that relationship is written in the intersection box.

questions.q: In a relationship matrix, what is the significance of the boxes lying on the diagonal?
o: They hold the primary key of each entity
They record the cardinality of each relationship
questions.e: Boxes on the diagonal pair an entity with itself, so they represent recursive relationships. Entries above the diagonal are the inverse, or mirror image, of the entries below it.

questions.q: In a relationship matrix, how do the entries above the diagonal line relate to those below it?
o: They are duplicates with identical names
Each is the inverse, or mirror image, of a relationship below the line
They record cardinality while the ones below record optionality
questions.e: Each relationship above the diagonal is the inverse or mirror image of a relationship below the line, since a relationship is bidirectional and each direction gets its own name.

questions.q: A relationship matrix records the following entries: CUSTOMER row and ORDER column reads 'place'; ORDER row and CUSTOMER column reads 'placed by'. What does this pair of entries represent?
o: Two separate relationships between the same entities
The two named perspectives of a single relationship
A mandatory relationship in one direction only
questions.e: 'Place' and 'placed by' are the two perspectives of one bidirectional relationship between CUSTOMER and ORDER, which is why one appears above the diagonal and the other below it.

questions.q: A relationship matrix covering CUSTOMER, ITEM, ORDER, and WAREHOUSE shows 'stored in' where the ITEM row meets the WAREHOUSE column. Which entry appears where the WAREHOUSE row meets the ITEM column?
questions.e: The mirror-image perspective of 'item stored in warehouse' is 'warehouse store item', so 'store' occupies the reversed intersection.

questions.q: A relationship matrix covering CUSTOMER, ITEM, ORDER, and WAREHOUSE leaves the intersection of the CUSTOMER row and the WAREHOUSE column empty. What does this tell you?
o: Customers and warehouses have a recursive relationship
No relationship has been identified between CUSTOMER and WAREHOUSE
The relationship exists but is optional
questions.e: An empty intersection box records that the row entity is not related to the column entity, so no CUSTOMER to WAREHOUSE relationship has been identified. Optionality would still require a named relationship in the box.

questions.q: A relationship matrix covering ACTIVITY, DEPARTMENT, and EMPLOYEE names the EMPLOYEE-to-ACTIVITY direction 'participate in'. Which name is given to the reverse ACTIVITY-to-EMPLOYEE direction?
questions.e: The ACTIVITY row and EMPLOYEE column carries 'assigned to', the mirror perspective of employees participating in activities. 'Contain' names the DEPARTMENT-to-EMPLOYEE direction in the same matrix.

questions.q: An ERD shows DEPARTMENT and EMPLOYEE joined by a line that is dashed on the DEPARTMENT half and solid on the EMPLOYEE half, with a crow's foot at the EMPLOYEE end and a plain ending at the DEPARTMENT end. Which pair of business rules does this express?
o: Each department must contain one and only one employee; each employee may be assigned to one or more departments
Each department may contain one or more employees; each employee must be assigned to one and only one department
Each department must contain one or more employees; each employee may be assigned to one and only one department
Each department may contain one and only one employee; each employee must be assigned to one or more departments
questions.e: The dashed half beside DEPARTMENT makes that perspective optional ('may'), and the crow's foot at the EMPLOYEE end makes it 'one or more'. The solid half beside EMPLOYEE makes that perspective mandatory ('must'), and the plain ending at DEPARTMENT makes it 'one and only one'.

questions.q: Consider the rule 'Each PRODUCT must be classified by one and only one PRODUCT TYPE.' Which pair of diagram features encodes this rule?
o: A dashed line with a crow's foot at the PRODUCT TYPE end
A solid line with a plain single-toe ending at the PRODUCT TYPE end
A dashed line with a plain single-toe ending at the PRODUCT TYPE end
A solid line with a crow's foot at the PRODUCT TYPE end
questions.e: 'Must' requires a solid, mandatory line on that half, and 'one and only one' requires a plain single-toe ending rather than a crow's foot. The inverse rule, that each product type may classify one or more products, would be drawn dashed with a crow's foot.

questions.q: The database conceptual model can be used for further discussion between which of these groups?
o: Designers, database administrators, and application developers
End users, auditors, and regulators only
questions.e: The conceptual model facilitates discussion between designers, database administrators, and application developers. It is a communication and design tool, not aimed at hardware vendors or salespeople.

questions.q: A conceptual model describes entities and the highest-level relationships between them, but does NOT specify which of the following?
o: The attributes or unique identifier for each entity
The things of significance to the organization
questions.e: A conceptual model describes things of significance (entities) and the highest-level relationships, and may or may not include cardinality and nullability, but it does not specify the attributes or the unique identifier for each entity. Those are added in the logical model.

questions.q: In a conceptual model, which two properties may or may not be included?
questions.e: A conceptual model identifies the highest-level relationships between entities but may or may not include cardinality and nullability. Data types, precision, indexes, and views belong to the physical model.

questions.q: The logical data model is normally derived from which model?
questions.e: The logical data model is normally derived from a conceptual data model and describes the data in as much detail as possible without regard to physical implementation.

questions.q: Which of the following does a logical data model include that a conceptual model may omit?
o: All entities, attributes, UIDs, relationships, optionality, and cardinality
questions.e: The logical model includes all entities, attributes, UIDs and relationships as well as their optionality and cardinality, while still omitting physical implementation details such as table definitions, data types, indexes, and storage.

questions.q: What is the first step in creating a logical model?
questions.e: The steps to create a logical model are: identify entities, identify attributes (with optionality), identify unique identifiers, then determine relationships (with optionality and cardinality). Identifying entities comes first.

questions.q: In building a logical model, identifying unique identifiers comes immediately after which step?
questions.e: The order is identify entities, identify attributes, identify unique identifiers, then determine relationships. Unique identifiers are chosen right after attributes are identified.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four goals of entity relationship modeling?
o: Model information that is derivable from other modeled information
Ensure that information appears only once
Store the same information in multiple predictable places
questions.e: A goal of ER modeling is that information appears only once (no redundancy). The other goals are capturing all required information, modeling NO derivable information, and locating information in a predictable, logical place.

questions.q: According to the goals of ER modeling, information that is derivable from other already-modeled information should be:
o: Stored in a separate audit entity
Modeled only in the physical model
questions.e: One goal is to model NO information that is derivable from other information already modeled. Derived data is not stored because it can be computed from existing data.

questions.q: What does it mean for a logical data model to be 'implementation-free'?
o: It cannot be built in any database
It stays the same regardless of the type of database system eventually implemented
It contains no entities or attributes
questions.e: 'Implementation-free' means a good logical data model stays the same regardless of the type of database system (hierarchical, network, relational, etc.) that is eventually built on it.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the database types on which a logical ER model could be implemented?
questions.e: The database types include the ER model and hierarchical, network, and relational databases. The logical model is independent of which of these is eventually chosen.

questions.q: Besides listing entities, attributes, and relationships, the Entity Relationship Model provides background information such as:
o: Entity descriptions, data types, and constraints
questions.e: The ERM provides background information such as entity descriptions, data types, and constraints. It is derived from business specifications and does not require a diagram, though one is typically useful.

questions.q: Does an Entity Relationship Model require a diagram?
o: No, but a diagram is typically a very useful tool
Only when there are more than ten entities
questions.e: An ERM does not require a diagram, but the diagram is typically a very useful tool for communicating the model.

questions.q: What is ERDish?
o: A programming language for writing SQL queries
A file format for saving diagrams
The vocabulary used to clearly communicate the business rules captured on an ERD
questions.e: ERDish is the vocabulary used to clearly communicate the business rules captured on an ERD. It states relationships between entities by breaking each sentence into components.

questions.q: Reading an ERDish sentence for one side of a relationship, which component comes immediately after the optionality (must be / may be)?
questions.e: The ERDish components in order are: EACH, Entity A, OPTIONALITY (must be/may be), RELATIONSHIP NAME, CARDINALITY (one and only one/one or more), Entity B. The relationship name follows the optionality.

questions.q: In an ERD, a solid line on a relationship indicates which optionality?
questions.e: A solid line represents the 'must be' (mandatory) optionality, while a dotted line represents 'may be' (optional). 'One or more' and 'one and only one' are cardinalities, not optionalities.

questions.q: In ERD notation, a crow's foot at the end of a relationship line represents which cardinality?
questions.e: The crow's foot represents the 'one or more' cardinality, whereas a single toe represents 'one and only one'. 'Must be' is an optionality, not a cardinality.

questions.q: A single toe (a single line ending) on a relationship represents which cardinality?
questions.e: A single toe represents 'one and only one' cardinality; a crow's foot represents 'one or more'.

questions.q: A dotted (dashed) relationship line in an ERD represents which optionality?
questions.e: A dotted line represents 'may be' (optional) optionality; a solid line represents 'must be' (mandatory).

questions.q: Given the relationship 'Each BOOK must be written by one and only one AUTHOR, and each AUTHOR may be the author of one or more BOOK', which statement about an AUTHOR is correct?
o: An AUTHOR must be the author of exactly one BOOK
An AUTHOR must be the author of one or more BOOK
An AUTHOR may write only one BOOK
An AUTHOR may be the author of one or more BOOK
questions.e: The AUTHOR side is optional ('may be') with cardinality 'one or more', so an author may be the author of one or more books. The mandatory 'must be' and single-toe 'one and only one' apply to the BOOK side.

questions.q: An ERD can represent the data requirements of a business under which condition?
o: Only if a relational database is used
Only after the physical database is built
Regardless of the type of database used, and even in the absence of one
questions.e: An ERD can represent the data requirements of a business regardless of the type of database that is used, and even in the absence of one, because it is a graphical, implementation-free representation.

questions.q: An ACCOUNT entity has # Number, and its full unique identifier requires both ACCOUNT Number and BANK Number. How is this shown on the ERD?
o: A crow's foot on both ends
A bar on the relationship line
A diamond on the relationship line
questions.e: When a relationship contributes to a UID, it is shown with a bar on the relationship line (a barred relationship). A diamond indicates non-transferability, not UID contribution.

questions.q: A WORK ASSIGNMENT entity is uniquely identified through its relationships to EMPLOYEE (# ID) and PROJECT (# Number). What forms the UID of WORK ASSIGNMENT?
questions.e: An entity can be uniquely identified through multiple relationships; here the UID of WORK ASSIGNMENT is EMPLOYEE ID and PROJECT Number, represented using bars.

questions.q: In ER modeling, attributes describe:
questions.e: Attributes describe only entities. If an attribute appears to describe a relationship (such as Quantity on an order-product link), the relationship must be resolved into an entity.

questions.q: A M:M relationship is resolved by introducing what?
o: A new intersection entity with two 1:M barred relationships
questions.e: A M:M relationship is resolved with a new intersection entity and two 1:M barred relationships. The intersection entity holds the attributes (like quantity) that described the relationship.

questions.q: When a M:M between ORDER (# Number) and PRODUCT (# ID) is resolved with an ORDER ITEM intersection entity, what is the UID of ORDER ITEM?
questions.e: The intersection entity ORDER ITEM is identified by its two originating relationships, so its UID is ORDER Number and PRODUCT ID.

questions.q: The relationships from an intersection entity to its originating entities are always:
questions.e: The relationships from an intersection entity are always mandatory. The intersection entity is identified by these two originating (identifying) relationships.

questions.q: Intersection entities usually contain which kind of data?
o: Consumables like quantity used and dates, and they tend to be high-volume and volatile
questions.e: Intersection entities usually contain consumables like quantity used and dates, and they tend to be high-volume and volatile entities.

questions.q: Transferability of a relationship is:
o: The ability of the relationship between two instances of an entity to change over time
The ability to convert a M:M to 1:M
The ability to inherit attributes from a supertype
questions.e: Transferability is the ability of the relationship between two instances of an entity to change over time. A non-transferable relationship cannot be moved between instances.

questions.q: How is a non-transferable relationship represented on an ERD?
questions.e: A non-transferable relationship is represented by a diamond on the relationship. A bar indicates a UID contribution, and a circle appears on arc relationships.

questions.q: A non-transferable relationship can only be:
questions.e: Non-transferable relationships can only be mandatory. For example, the birth country of a person is non-transferable.

questions.q: A supertype has what kind of relationship with its subtypes?
o: A parent-child relationship with one or more subtypes
questions.e: A supertype has a parent-child relationship with one or more subtypes. Each subtype is a specialization drawn within the supertype.

questions.q: Where must the common attributes and relationships shared by all subtypes be listed?
o: Only in the supertype, but they are inherited by every subtype
questions.e: Common attributes and relationships for all subtypes must be listed only in the supertype, but they are inherited in every subtype.

questions.q: Which statement about subtypes is true?
o: There can never be just one subtype; another must exist to contain the rest
An entity can have exactly one subtype
A subtype cannot have its own attributes
questions.e: There can never be just one subtype; another subtype should be created to contain the rest. A subtype can also have its own attributes and relationships and can be nested.

questions.q: Regarding primary keys, a subtype:
o: Has a completely different primary key from the supertype
Has identical primary keys of the supertype and subtype
questions.e: A subtype has identical primary keys of the supertype and subtype. It also inherits all attributes and relationships of the supertype and never exists alone.

questions.q: Generalization is best described as:
o: A bottom-up approach that combines two or more lower-level entities into a higher-level entity based on common features
A top-down approach that breaks a higher-level entity into lower-level entities
Adding a bar to a relationship
questions.e: Generalization is a bottom-up approach where two or more lower-level entities are combined to form a higher-level entity based on common features (for example, CAR and TRUCK into VEHICLE).

questions.q: Specialization is best described as:
o: A top-down approach where a higher-level entity is broken down into lower-level entities
questions.e: Specialization is a top-down approach where the higher-level entity is broken down into lower-level entities (for example, EMPLOYEE into CURRENT EMPLOYEE and EX-EMPLOYEE).

questions.q: The subtype rule that 'every instance of a supertype is also an instance of one of the subtypes' is called:
questions.e: This is the exhaustive rule. To satisfy it, an OTHER subtype is often included to categorize instances not covered by existing subtypes.

questions.q: The rule that every instance of the supertype belongs to one and only one subtype is called:
questions.e: This is the mutually exclusive rule, for example an employee cannot be both full time and part time. The exhaustive rule instead requires every instance to fall into some subtype.

questions.q: A recursive relationship is one where:
o: Two different entities share a M:M relationship
A subtype inherits from a supertype
An entity instance is related to another instance in the same entity
questions.e: A recursive relationship is one where an entity instance is related to another instance in the same entity (for example, an EMPLOYEE managed by another EMPLOYEE). It is always modeled with a loop.

questions.q: Modeling a Bill of Materials with a single generic COMPONENT entity related to itself creates what kind of relationship?
questions.e: Using a generic COMPONENT entity to model a Bill of Materials creates a recursive M:M relationship, which is then resolved with an intersection entity such as ASSEMBLY RULE.

questions.q: An arc relationship is:
o: An exclusive relationship group in which only one of the relationships can exist for any instance of an entity
A relationship that changes over time
A relationship that contributes to a UID
A parent-child relationship between supertype and subtype
questions.e: An arc is an exclusive relationship group defined such that only one of the relationships can exist for any instance of an entity; it implies an 'or' condition and demonstrates mutual exclusivity.

questions.q: The relationships within a single arc must be:
o: A mix of mandatory and optional
Either all mandatory or all optional, and should have the same cardinality
questions.e: The relationships in an arc must be either all mandatory or all optional and should have the same cardinality. They also frequently share the same relationship name.

questions.q: Which statement about arcs is correct?
o: A single relationship can participate in multiple arcs
An arc can include relationships from several different entities
An entity may have multiple arcs, but a specific relationship can participate in only a single arc
An arc always implies an 'and' condition
questions.e: An entity may have multiple arcs, but a specific relationship can participate only in a single arc. An arc belongs to a single entity and includes only relationships originating from that entity.

questions.q: Relationships included in an arc are marked on the relationship line with:
questions.e: Relationships included in the arc have a circle on the relationship arc line, and the arc itself is drawn as an arc-shaped line across two or more relationship lines.

questions.q: Hierarchical data is represented in an ERD as:
o: A set of 1:M relationships, with UIDs propagated through multiple barred relationships
A M:M relationship resolved by an arc
A supertype with mutually exclusive subtypes
questions.e: Hierarchical data is represented as a set of 1:M relationships, and the UIDs for the set of hierarchical entities can be propagated through multiple barred relationships.

questions.q: Why do most businesses need to track some historical data?
o: To help find trends and patterns that can be the basis for business innovations or process improvements
questions.e: Most businesses track historical data to help find trends and patterns that can form the basis for business innovations or process improvements.

questions.q: In data-over-time modeling, what happens with every update of an attribute or transfer of a relationship?
o: An audit trail is automatically created
It means a loss of information
questions.e: Every update of an attribute or transfer of a relationship means a loss of information. Some systems must therefore keep historical values or an audit trail of each transaction.

questions.q: Why should requirements for storing historical data be validated with the user?
o: Because historical data cannot be queried
Because storing unnecessary historical data can be costly
Because history always requires a M:M relationship
Because audit trails are illegal in some industries
questions.e: Requirements for storing historical data should be validated with the user because storing unnecessary historical data can be costly.

questions.q: Which of the following is a question used to decide whether to add entities or relationships for historical data?
o: Can attribute values change over time?
Which programming language will query it?
questions.e: The modeling questions include: Is an audit trail required? Can attribute values change over time? Can relationships change over time? Do you need to query older data? Index and tablespace choices are physical concerns, not modeling questions.

questions.q: If you need to track only the current status of a contract (ID, description, status, effective date), how many entities are needed?
o: Two entities plus an intersection entity
questions.e: Use one entity if you track only the current status of a contract. To store the status of a contract over time, you add a second entity (such as CONTRACT STATUS).

questions.q: To store the status of a contract over time rather than just its current status, you should:
o: Add more attributes to the single CONTRACT entity
Add an additional entity (such as CONTRACT STATUS) to track the values over time
questions.e: To track attribute values over time, create additional entities. Adding a CONTRACT STATUS entity (with effective date and current value) stores the status of a contract over time.

questions.q: A simple 'PERSON rent APARTMENT' relationship does not allow tracking of what?
o: The date that an apartment is rented
questions.e: The direct rent relationship does not allow tracking of the date that an apartment is rented. Adding a RENTAL entity captures the rental relationship (with effective and renewal dates) over time.

questions.q: To accommodate a relationship that may change over time (such as who rents an apartment), you should:
o: Add an entity (such as RENTAL) to capture the relationship over time
Add a diamond to make it non-transferable
questions.e: To accommodate a relationship that may change over time, add an entity, for example a RENTAL entity with an effective date and renewal date, to capture the relationship over time.

questions.q: Resolving a M:M relationship with an intersection entity is frequently used to:
o: Track information about a relationship that changes over time
questions.e: Resolving a M:M relationship with an intersection entity is frequently used to track information about a relationship that changes over time, storing the history in the intersection entity.

questions.q: A direct 'EMPLOYEE hold JOB' relationship fails to store what?
o: The history of an employee's jobs
questions.e: The direct relationship does not store the history of an employee's jobs. Resolving the M:M and adding a JOB HISTORY intersection entity (with start date and end date) stores the historical information.

questions.q: In a JOB HISTORY intersection entity used to record an employee's past jobs, which attributes capture the time period?
questions.e: The JOB HISTORY intersection entity stores Start Date and End Date to capture the period an employee held a job. Minimum/Maximum Salary and Title belong to the JOB entity.

questions.q: A PAYMENT MODIFICATION entity that stores 'Previous Amount', 'Modified by', and 'Modification Date' is an example of:
o: Using additional entities and attributes to log modified information about how a payment changes over time
questions.e: Additional entities and attributes can store modified information; the PAYMENT MODIFICATION entity logs how a payment changes over time using previous amount, who modified it, and the modification date.

questions.q: A jewelry store's ERD tracks only the current renter of each item but now wants the full rental history. The relationship between JEWELRY DETAIL and CUSTOMER should first be changed to:
questions.e: To track rental history, the relationship between JEWELRY DETAIL and CUSTOMER is changed to M:M, which is then resolved with an intersection entity (RENTAL HISTORY).

questions.q: After making the jewelry rental relationship M:M, how is it resolved to record each rental's dates?
o: With a RENTAL HISTORY intersection entity holding the date rented and date returned
questions.e: The M:M is resolved with a RENTAL HISTORY intersection entity that records the date rented (date on) and date returned, capturing the rental history.

questions.q: What is the primary modeling objective addressed when adding entities such as JOB HISTORY, RENTAL, and PAYMENT MODIFICATION?
o: Keeping track of data that changes over time
questions.e: These additional entities all serve the objective of keeping track of data that changes over time, preserving historical values that a simple current-state model would lose.

questions.q: What is normalization in the context of a relational database?
o: The process of adding redundant copies of data to speed up queries
The process of encrypting sensitive columns before storage
The process of converting a relational design back into an ERD
The process of organizing the attributes and tables to minimize redundancy
questions.e: Normalization is the process of organizing the attributes and tables of a relational database to minimize redundancy. It is the opposite of deliberately adding redundant copies, and it operates on the design of tables/attributes rather than encrypting data or reverse-engineering an ERD.

questions.q: Normalization helps a database handle which of the following?
questions.e: Normalization helps in handling insert, update, and delete anomalies, ensuring better database performance. It targets data-consistency anomalies, not networking, security/authentication, or backup concerns.

questions.q: To which normal form should data be normalized before transforming the model into a relational design?
questions.e: The goal is to normalize data to 3NF before transforming the model into the relational design. 1NF and 2NF are intermediate stages, and BCNF is not part of the three main normal forms addressed here.

questions.q: Who introduced the main types of normal forms (1NF, 2NF, and 3NF)?
questions.e: The main normal forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF) were introduced by E. F. Codd. Peter Chen is associated with entity-relationship modeling and Bachman with early data structures, but the normal forms are Codd's.

questions.q: Which rule correctly states the requirement of First Normal Form (1NF)?
o: No non-UID attribute can depend on another non-UID attribute
Every attribute must depend on the entire UID
Every table must have a foreign key
questions.e: First Normal Form requires that all attributes be single-valued (no multi-valued attributes). Dependence on the entire UID is 2NF, and prohibiting non-UID-to-non-UID dependencies is 3NF.

questions.q: Which statement describes the requirement of Second Normal Form (2NF)?
o: All attributes must have a single value
No non-UID attribute can depend on another non-UID attribute
An attribute must be dependent on its entity's entire UID
Every relationship must be resolved into an intersection entity
questions.e: 2NF requires that any non-UID attribute be dependent on the entity's entire UID. Single-valued attributes is the 1NF rule, and the ban on non-UID-to-non-UID dependencies is the 3NF rule.

questions.q: Which statement describes the rule of Third Normal Form (3NF)?
o: All multi-valued attributes must be split into a 1:M relationship
Each attribute must depend on part of a composite UID
No non-UID attribute can be dependent on another non-UID attribute
questions.e: 3NF states that no non-UID attribute can be dependent on another non-UID attribute, which prohibits transitive dependencies. Single-valued attributes is 1NF, and dependence on the entire UID is 2NF.

questions.q: Third Normal Form specifically prohibits which kind of dependency?
o: Partial dependency on a composite UID
questions.e: 3NF prohibits transitive dependencies, which exist when a non-UID attribute depends on another non-UID attribute in the same entity. Partial dependency on part of a composite UID is a 2NF concern, not 3NF.

questions.q: An attribute is found to be multi-valued for each instance of an entity. What corrective action puts the model into 1NF?
o: Delete the attribute from the entity
Create an additional entity and relate it to the original with a 1:M relationship
Merge the attribute into the UID
Convert the attribute into a foreign key of the same entity
questions.e: To achieve 1NF, a multi-valued attribute is placed in an additional entity related to the original by a 1:M relationship. Deleting the attribute loses data, and merging it into the UID or making it a foreign key of the same entity does not remove the repetition.

questions.q: If an entity has a composite UID, what does 2NF require of every non-UID attribute?
o: It must depend on all parts of the composite UID
It must depend on only one part of the composite UID
It must not depend on any part of the UID
It must be moved to a separate table regardless of dependency
questions.e: With a composite UID, 2NF requires each non-UID attribute to depend on all parts of the composite UID. An attribute dependent on only part of the UID violates 2NF and should be moved to a new entity with that partial UID.

questions.q: An ACCOUNT entity has attributes Balance, Name, Date Opened, and Bank Location, where Bank Location actually depends on the account's bank rather than the account itself. Which normal form is violated and how is it fixed?
o: 1NF is violated; make Bank Location single-valued
1NF is violated; create a 1:M relationship for Bank Location
2NF is violated; move Bank Location to a BANK entity
questions.e: Bank Location depends on BANK, not on ACCOUNT's UID, so this violates 2NF (an attribute not dependent on the entity's entire UID). The fix is to move Bank Location to the BANK entity where it belongs.

questions.q: An ORDER entity (UID = ID) also holds Line Item ID, Quantity, and Price, where Quantity and Price depend on both the order ID and the non-UID Line Item ID. What resolves this into 3NF?
o: Add Line Item ID to the ORDER primary key
Create a new ORDER ITEM entity and move Line Item ID, Quantity, and Price into it with an identifying relationship
Delete the Quantity and Price attributes
questions.e: Quantity and Price depend on the non-UID Line Item ID, a transitive dependency that violates 3NF. The fix is to create a new ORDER ITEM entity, move Line Item ID, Quantity, and Price there, and create an identifying relationship to ORDER.

questions.q: A CLIENT entity records Date Contacted and Contact Details, each of which can have multiple values per client. Which normal form does this violate?
questions.e: Because Date Contacted and Contact Details have multiple values for a single client, the entity violates 1NF, which requires single-valued attributes. The fix is to create a separate CONTACT entity with a 1:M relationship to CLIENT.

questions.q: What is a business rule?
o: A statement that defines or constrains some aspect of the business
A SQL statement that creates a constraint in the database
A physical index that speeds up query performance
A report generated after normalization is complete
questions.e: A business rule is a statement that defines or constrains some aspect of the business, and is used to define entities, attributes, relationships, and constraints. It is a conceptual statement about how the business operates, not a SQL constraint or physical index.

questions.q: What are the two types of business rules?
questions.e: Business rules are classified as structural and procedural. Structural rules describe what information is stored and how it interrelates; procedural rules deal with prerequisites, steps, and workflow, often related to time.

questions.q: Which of the following is identified as a source of business rules?
questions.e: Sources of business rules include top management and managers, written documentation (procedures, standards, operations manuals), and direct interviews with end users. The query optimizer and storage engine are not sources of business rules.

questions.q: Which characteristic applies to structural business rules?
o: They deal with the order in which events must occur
They detail a static aspect of the business and can always be diagrammed in the ERD
They always require additional programming and cannot be diagrammed
They describe time-based prerequisites between events
questions.e: Structural business rules describe the types of information stored and how elements interrelate; they detail a static aspect of the business and can always be diagrammed in the ERD. Time-based, order-of-events rules are procedural, not structural.

questions.q: A rule states that a next-day delivery order cannot be accepted if it is received after 3:00 PM. What kind of business rule is this?
questions.e: This is a procedural business rule because it concerns a time-based prerequisite (the order's timing) and a workflow condition. Procedural rules deal with steps, processes, and time; many cannot be diagrammed and must be documented for later programming.

questions.q: Why might a rule such as 'any employee whose overtime exceeds 10 hours per week must be paid 1.5 times the hourly rate' not be captured directly in a conceptual data model?
o: Because it is a structural rule that belongs only in the physical model
Because it is a naming-convention rule
Because it violates Third Normal Form
Because it must be implemented by programming as a process that interacts with the data
questions.e: Some rules cannot be modeled in the conceptual data model and must be implemented by programming as processes that interact with the data. This overtime-pay rule is such a procedural rule, unlike structural rules that can be diagrammed in the ERD.

questions.q: Which of the following is a stated reason for normalizing data?
o: To identify missing tables, columns, and constraints
To increase redundant data for faster reads
To remove all foreign keys from the design
To bypass the need for business rules
questions.e: Reasons to normalize include reducing redundant data, increasing integrity and design stability, eliminating inconsistencies and anomalies, and identifying missing tables, columns, and constraints. Normalization reduces redundancy rather than increasing it.

questions.q: Although normalization is a relational database concept, how do its principles relate to data modeling?
o: They do not apply to data modeling at all
They apply only after the physical model is built
Its principles apply to data modeling as well
They apply only to procedural business rules
questions.e: Normalization is a relational database concept, but its principles also apply to data modeling, which is why the goal is to normalize to 3NF before transforming the model to the relational design.

questions.q: In the mapping from an ERD to a physical design, an entity becomes which physical object?
questions.e: An entity maps to a table. Within that mapping, an instance maps to a row and an attribute maps to a column, so entity-to-table is the correct correspondence.

questions.q: In the ERD-to-physical terminology mapping, an instance of an entity corresponds to what?
questions.e: An instance maps to a row in the physical design. An attribute maps to a column and the entity itself maps to a table, so an individual instance is a row.

questions.q: A Primary UID in the ERD maps to which object in the physical design?
questions.e: A Primary UID maps to a Primary Key. By contrast, a Secondary UID maps to a Unique Key and a relationship maps to a Foreign Key.

questions.q: A Secondary UID in a logical model maps to which structure in the physical model?
questions.e: A Secondary UID maps to a Unique Key. The Primary UID maps to the Primary Key, and relationships map to Foreign Keys.

questions.q: A relationship in the ERD maps to which object in the physical design?
questions.e: A relationship maps to a Foreign Key, which lets one table reference another. Primary UID maps to primary key and secondary UID maps to unique key.

questions.q: According to the naming conventions, how is a table name derived from its entity name?
o: It is the singular of the entity name
It is the plural of the entity name
It is the entity name with a numeric suffix
It is an abbreviation of the entity name in lowercase
questions.e: The table name is the plural of the entity name; for example the entity STUDENT becomes the table STUDENTS. It is not a singular form, numeric suffix, or lowercase abbreviation.

questions.q: How are column names derived from attribute names under the naming conventions?
o: They are identical except that special characters and spaces are replaced with underscores
They must always be a fixed three-letter abbreviation
They are the plural form of the attribute name
questions.e: Column names are identical to attribute names except that special characters and spaces are replaced with underscores (for example, 'first name' becomes 'first_name'). Columns often use more abbreviations than attributes, but a fixed three-letter form is not required.

questions.q: The attribute 'street address' is being mapped to a physical column. What is the resulting column name under the naming conventions?
questions.e: Spaces in an attribute name are replaced with underscores, so 'street address' becomes 'street_address'. Hyphens are not used, and the space is not simply removed.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of assigning a unique short name to every table?
o: To satisfy the 30-character limit for table names
To replace the plural table name in queries
To act as the table's primary key
To use when naming foreign-key columns
questions.e: A unique short name for every table is useful when naming foreign-key columns; the short name of the referenced table is used to form the FK column name. It is not the primary key nor a replacement for the table name itself.

questions.q: Which of the following is a basis for creating a table short name?
o: Entity names that contain more than one word
Entity names that are already fewer than three characters
Entity names that appear only once in the model
Entity names that have no primary key
questions.e: Short names are created based on entity names that contain more than one word, one word with more than one syllable, or one syllable with more than one character. The other options are not listed criteria.

questions.q: Under Oracle naming restrictions, what is true about table and column names?
o: They can contain up to 30 alphanumeric characters
They may start with a number or a letter
They may contain spaces if enclosed in quotes
They may be reserved words if capitalized
questions.e: Table and column names can contain up to 30 alphanumeric characters. They must start with a letter (not a number), cannot contain spaces, and cannot be reserved words.

questions.q: Which special characters are permitted in Oracle table and column names?
questions.e: The permitted special characters are $, #, and _ (underscore). Characters such as '!' are not allowed, and names cannot contain spaces.

questions.q: Which uniqueness rule applies to Oracle table and column names?
o: Table names must be unique across the entire database instance
Table names may be reused within the same user account
Column names must be unique across all tables
Column names must be unique within a table
questions.e: Column names must be unique within a table, and table names must be unique within one user account. Column names need not be globally unique across all tables, and table names cannot be reused within the same account.

questions.q: When a 1:M relationship is mapped, where is the foreign-key column created?
o: In the table on the one side of the relationship
In the table on the many side of the relationship
questions.e: A relationship creates one or more foreign-key columns in the table on the many side of the relationship. The FK references the primary key of the table on the one side, but the column itself lives on the many side.

questions.q: In an EMPLOYEES table, a foreign key to DEPARTMENT is named dpt_id and a recursive foreign key to itself is named mgr_id. What naming principle does this illustrate?
o: Foreign-key columns use the short name of the referenced table
Foreign-key columns must match the primary key name exactly
Foreign-key columns are always named after the many-side table
Recursive relationships cannot be given foreign-key columns
questions.e: The foreign-key column is named using the short name of the referenced table (dpt for DEPARTMENT, and mgr as the role short name for the recursive manager relationship). Recursive relationships can indeed have FK columns, and the FK need not copy the PK name exactly.

questions.q: What is distinctive about the foreign-key column produced when mapping a barred relationship?
o: It is created on the one side of the relationship
It plays a double role because it is also part of the primary key
It replaces the primary key of the table entirely
questions.e: In a barred relationship, the foreign-key column on the many side also forms part of the primary key, so it plays a double role. For example, bak_nbr in ACCOUNTS is both a foreign key to BANKS and part of the ACCOUNTS primary key.

questions.q: How is a many-to-many (M:M) relationship resolved during mapping?
o: By creating a foreign key on the stronger entity only
By making both primary keys optional
By merging the two entities into one table
By resolving it with an intersection entity that maps to an intersection table
questions.e: A M:M relationship is resolved with an intersection entity that maps to an intersection table containing foreign-key columns referring to the originating tables. For example, a REVIEWS table holds ctc_id and mve_id for the CRITIC-MOVIE relationship.

questions.q: In the intersection table REVIEWS that resolves a M:M relationship between CRITIC and MOVIE, how are the columns ctc_id and mve_id typically defined?
o: As part of the primary key and each also a foreign key
As unique keys only, with no foreign keys
questions.e: In the REVIEWS intersection table, ctc_id and mve_id are each part of the primary key and are also foreign keys (pk,fk1 and pk,fk2) referring to the CRITICS and MOVIES tables. They form a composite primary key, not two separate primary keys.

questions.q: When transforming a 1:1 relationship, what two things are created for the mapped column?
o: A foreign key and a unique key
A primary key and a check constraint
A foreign key and an index only
questions.e: Mapping a 1:1 relationship creates a foreign key and a unique key, with all columns of the foreign key also part of the unique key. For example, cbe_code in EMPLOYEES is both a foreign key to CUBICLES and unique within EMPLOYEES.

questions.q: When mapping an arc (exclusive) relationship, why must the resulting foreign-key columns be optional even if the relationships are mandatory on the many side?
o: Because one of the foreign keys will always be blank
Because arcs cannot use foreign keys
Because the primary key forbids mandatory foreign keys
questions.e: In an arc, only one of the exclusive relationships applies to a given row, so one of the foreign keys will always be blank; therefore the FKs must be optional. A check constraint enforces that exactly one is populated.

questions.q: In a single-table implementation of a supertype/subtype structure, how are the subtype attributes' columns defined?
o: They are omitted from the table
questions.e: In a single-table implementation, supertype attribute columns keep their original optionality, but the subtype attribute columns all become optional. A mandatory discriminator column is added to distinguish the subtypes.

questions.q: What additional column must be created in a single-table implementation of supertypes and subtypes?
o: A foreign key to each subtype table
A unique key spanning all subtype attributes
A mandatory discriminator column to distinguish the subtypes
A separate primary key for each subtype
questions.e: A single-table implementation requires a mandatory discriminator column (for example, epe_type) to distinguish between the different subtypes stored in the one table. There are no separate subtype tables in this approach.

questions.q: When is a single-table implementation preferred for a supertype/subtype structure?
o: When subtypes have little in common and few shared attributes
When each subtype needs its own primary key
When there are more than two subtypes
When most of the attributes and relationships are shared at the supertype level
questions.e: A single-table implementation is used when most of the attributes and relationships are shared and therefore at the supertype level. When subtypes have little in common, a two-table (per-subtype) implementation is used instead.

questions.q: In a two-table implementation of a supertype/subtype structure, how many tables are created?
o: Exactly two tables regardless of the number of subtypes
One table for the supertype and one shared table for all subtypes
One table combining the supertype and all subtypes
questions.e: The two-table implementation creates one table per first-level subtype (so there can be more than two tables). Each such table gets a column for each supertype attribute and each subtype attribute, keeping their original optionality.

questions.q: In which file format does Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler store metadata information?
questions.e: Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler stores metadata information in XML files. It can also synchronize the relational model with the data dictionary, but the metadata store is XML.

questions.q: Which capability is provided by Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler?
o: Synchronizing the relational model with the data dictionary
Automatically writing business procedures in Java
Encrypting all model files by default
questions.e: Data Modeler can capture business rules, create process/logical/relational/physical models, store metadata in XML, and synchronize the relational model with the data dictionary. It is a modeling tool, not a database server or code generator for business procedures.

questions.q: What is the first step in building an ERD in Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler?
questions.e: The first step is to navigate to the Logical tab, after which the toolbar changes to display ERD-specific tools. Creating entities, adding attributes, and defining relationships are later steps.

questions.q: If the Logical tab is not visible, how do you display it?
o: Create a new entity to force the tab open
Right-click the Logical Model in the browser and select Show
questions.e: If the Logical tab is not visible, right-click the Logical Model in the browser and select Show. This reveals the tab without reinstalling or resetting anything.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the core steps for building an entity relationship diagram in Data Modeler?
o: Navigate to Logical tab, create entity, add attributes, set UIDs, define relationship
Create entity, navigate to Logical tab, define relationship, add attributes, set UIDs
Add attributes, create entity, set UIDs, navigate to Logical tab, define relationship
Navigate to Logical tab, define relationship, create entity, add attributes, set UIDs
questions.e: The core sequence is: navigate to the Logical tab, create an entity, add attributes to the entity, set the unique identifiers, then define the relationship between the entities. Attributes and UIDs must exist before relationships are defined.

questions.q: After clicking the New Entity tool, where do you click to open the Entity Properties window?
o: Anywhere in the white space of the Logical pane
questions.e: After selecting the New Entity tool, you click anywhere in the white space of the Logical pane, which creates the entity and opens the Entity Properties window. You do not click an existing entity or switch to the Physical tab.

questions.q: Are data types required when adding attributes in the logical model, and what benefit do they provide if entered?
o: They are required and appear on the ERD
They are optional and have no further effect
They are required only for primary UID attributes
They are not required and will not appear on the ERD, but allow conversion to SQL data types when engineering to the physical model
questions.e: Data types are not required in the logical model and will not be shown on the ERD, but adding them lets Data Modeler convert them to actual SQL data types when engineering to the physical (relational) model. They apply to all attributes, not only the primary UID.

questions.q: Through which menu path can you set commonly used logical data types as preferred?
o: Tools > Preferences > Data Modeler, then select the Model node
questions.e: Preferred logical data types are set via Tools > Preferences > Data Modeler, selecting the Model node, then moving types from All Logical Types into the preferred area. Selecting the Preferred check box then limits the drop-down to those types.

questions.q: When you assign an attribute as the Primary UID of an entity, what happens automatically?
o: It is automatically set to mandatory
It is automatically converted to a foreign key
It is automatically hidden from the ERD
It automatically becomes a secondary UID as well
questions.e: The attribute assigned as the Primary UID is automatically also set to mandatory. It does not become a foreign key or a secondary UID, and it remains visible on the diagram.

questions.q: To begin adding a Secondary UID, which node do you select in the left navigator of the Entity Properties window?
questions.e: To set a Secondary UID you select Unique Identifiers in the left navigator, then use the Add icon to add another UID. Selecting Attributes is how you set the Primary UID, not a secondary one.

questions.q: Which set of relationship types is available in Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler?
questions.e: The available relationship types are 1:1 (one-to-one), 1:N (one-to-many), 1:N Identifying (one-to-many barred), and M:N (many-to-many). 'Transitive' is not a relationship type in the tool.

questions.q: After clicking a relationship type on the toolbar, how is the relationship created between two entities?
o: Click the target entity and then the source entity
Drag the primary key onto the other entity
Click the source entity and then the target entity
questions.e: You click the source entity and then click the target entity to create the relationship. The order matters because it establishes source and target; double-clicking or dragging a key is not the method.

questions.q: How do you display the source and target relationship names on the diagram?
o: Double-click the relationship and enable Names
Right-click the diagram whitespace, select Show, then click Labels
Right-click the entity and select Rename
questions.e: To display source and target relationship names, right-click the diagram whitespace, select Show, then click Labels. Naming the relationship is done in its properties, but showing the labels uses the Show > Labels menu.

questions.q: How do you change the path of a relationship line in Data Modeler?
o: Right-click the relationship, select Add elbow, and drag the center handle
Double-click the line and enter coordinates
Right-click the entity and select Move line
questions.e: To reshape a relationship line, right-click the relationship, select Add elbow, then drag the center handle to the desired position. There is no need to delete and redraw the relationship.

questions.q: To make an entity a subtype of a supertype, what must exist first, and how is the subtype assigned?
o: The subtype must exist first; select it from the Sub Type list
A relationship must be drawn between them before subtyping
Both must be merged into one entity before assigning
The supertype must exist first; double-click the subtype entity and select the supertype from the Super Type list
questions.e: The supertype must already exist. You double-click the entity you want to make a subtype and select the supertype from the Super Type list; the subtype then inherits all attributes of the supertype.

questions.q: What does a subtype entity inherit from its supertype when created in Data Modeler?
o: All the attributes of the supertype
Only the relationships, not the attributes
questions.e: Once an entity is made a subtype, it inherits all the attributes of the supertype, in addition to having its own specific attributes. It inherits more than just the primary UID.

questions.q: What steps create an arc (exclusive) relationship in Data Modeler?
o: Draw a single relationship and mark it exclusive in properties
Hold the Ctrl key, select the intersecting entity and both relationships, then click the New Arc icon
Right-click the entity and select New Arc
Select M:N from the toolbar and click each entity
questions.e: To create an arc, hold the Ctrl key, select the intersecting entity and both relationships involved, then click the New Arc icon on the toolbar. This produces the exclusive relationship with the arc.

questions.q: Which toolbar option is used to create a barred relationship?
questions.e: A barred relationship is added by selecting Identifying Relationship from the toolbar and clicking the source and target entities. The New Arc icon creates exclusive arcs, not barred relationships.

questions.q: How is hierarchical data represented in Data Modeler, and how are the UIDs propagated through the hierarchy?
o: As M:N relationships, with UIDs propagated by intersection tables
As 1:1 relationships, with UIDs merged manually
As recursive relationships only, with UIDs never propagated
As a set of 1:N (or 1:N Identifying) relationships, with UIDs propagated by making the relationships Identifying
questions.e: Hierarchical data is represented as a set of 1:N relationships (or 1:N Identifying). The UIDs of a set of hierarchical entities are propagated through multiple relationships by making the relationships Identifying.

questions.q: How do you create a recursive relationship in Data Modeler after selecting the relationship type from the toolbar?
o: Click the entity to make it the source, then click the same entity a second time to make it the target
Click two different entities in sequence
Hold Ctrl and click the entity once
Double-click the entity and select Recursive
questions.e: For a recursive relationship, select the relationship from the toolbar, click the entity to make it the source, then click the same entity a second time to make it the target. Both source and target are the same entity.

questions.q: Which data modeling approach is used when designing a brand-new database that does not yet exist?
questions.e: Top-down modeling is the approach taken for designing a new database. Bottom-up modeling instead starts from an existing database (metadata or DDL), and target modeling is used for adapting a database to new requirements.

questions.q: Which modeling approach is taken when creating a database by extracting metadata from an existing database or from DDL code obtained from an existing implementation?
questions.e: Bottom-up modeling builds a model from an existing database, using extracted metadata or DDL. Top-down modeling is for designing a new database, and target modeling is for adapting an existing database to new requirements.

questions.q: Which of the three data modeling approaches is best suited for adapting a database to new requirements?
questions.e: Target modeling is best suited for adapting a database to new requirements. Top-down modeling designs a new database, and bottom-up modeling derives a model from an existing database's metadata or DDL.

questions.q: What is forward engineering in the context of data modeling?
o: Creating a logical model by extracting information from an existing data source
Generating DDL from a completed physical database
Adapting an existing database to new business requirements
Transforming a logical data model into a relational model
questions.e: Forward engineering is the process of transforming a logical data model into a relational model. Creating a model by extracting information from an existing data source is reverse engineering, which works in the opposite direction.

questions.q: What is reverse engineering in the context of data modeling?
o: Creating a conceptual or logical model by extracting information from an existing data source
Transforming a logical data model into a relational model
Adapting a database to new requirements
Converting attribute names into column names
questions.e: Reverse engineering creates a conceptual or logical model by extracting information from an existing data source. Transforming a logical model into a relational model is the opposite process, forward engineering.

questions.q: In Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler, a physical model is represented by which type of model?
questions.e: In Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler a physical model is represented by a Relational Model. The logical and conceptual models are earlier, more abstract stages of the design.

questions.q: When a logical model is converted to a relational model, an entity becomes which relational object?
questions.e: An entity in the logical model maps to a table in the relational model. Attributes map to columns and instances map to rows, so those are the confusable alternatives.

questions.q: When converting a logical model to a relational model, an attribute maps to which relational object?
questions.e: An attribute in the logical model maps to a column in the relational model. An entity maps to a table and an instance maps to a row, which are the common points of confusion.

questions.q: In the mapping from a logical model to a relational model, a single instance of an entity corresponds to which relational element?
questions.e: An instance maps to a row in the relational model, because a row holds one occurrence of the entity's data. The entity itself maps to a table and each attribute maps to a column.

questions.q: A primary unique identifier (primary UID) in a logical model maps to which relational structure?
questions.e: A primary UID maps to a primary key in the relational model. A secondary UID instead maps to a unique constraint, and a relationship maps to a foreign key.

questions.q: A secondary unique identifier (secondary UID) in a logical model maps to which relational structure?
questions.e: A secondary UID maps to a unique constraint. The primary UID maps to the primary key, so that is the distractor students most often pick.

questions.q: A relationship in a logical model maps to which structure in the relational model?
questions.e: A relationship maps to a foreign key in the relational model, because foreign keys implement the links between tables. Business constraints, by contrast, map to check constraints.

questions.q: Business constraints from the logical model are implemented in the relational model as which type of constraint?
questions.e: Business constraints map to check constraints in the relational model. Relationships map to foreign keys and unique identifiers map to primary keys or unique constraints, so those are the confusable choices.

questions.q: Which of the following is a stated benefit of creating a relational model?
o: It removes the need for a physical database design
It forms the basis for the physical database design
It replaces the logical model entirely
It stores the actual production data
questions.e: A relational model forms the basis for the physical database design; it is also closer to the implementation solution and facilitates discussion. It supports the physical design rather than removing the need for it.

questions.q: In Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler, which action begins forward engineering a selected logical model into a relational model?
o: Clicking the Engineer to Logical Model icon
Clicking the Engineer to Relational Model icon
questions.e: After selecting the logical model you click the Engineer to Relational Model icon and then click Engineer. The Engineer to Logical Model icon performs the opposite (reverse) direction.

questions.q: Which icon is used to reverse engineer a selected relational model back into a logical model?
questions.e: To reverse engineer, you select the relational model and click the Engineer to Logical Model icon, then click Engineer. The Engineer to Relational Model icon does forward engineering instead.

questions.q: By convention, what is generally used as the table name that corresponds to an entity?
o: The plural of the entity name
The singular of the entity name
questions.e: The plural of the entity name is generally used as the corresponding table name. Abbreviations are instead used for table short names, which help name foreign key columns and constraints.

questions.q: Why must special characters such as %, *, #, and spaces be replaced (typically with an underscore) in column names?
o: Because they make column names longer
Because SQL does not allow most special characters in column names
Because they conflict with foreign key names
questions.e: Special characters are replaced (commonly with an underscore) because SQL does not allow most special characters to be used in column names. Column names are otherwise often identical to the attribute names.

questions.q: A unique abbreviation defined for every table (a table short name) is especially useful for naming which of the following?
o: Foreign key columns or foreign key constraints
questions.e: A unique table short name (abbreviation) is a useful element for naming foreign key columns and foreign key constraints. It is not primarily about primary key columns or check constraints.

questions.q: According to Oracle Database naming restrictions, what must a table or column name begin with?
questions.e: Table and column names must start with a letter. They may contain up to 30 alphanumeric characters, must not contain spaces or certain special characters, and must avoid reserved words.

questions.q: Under Oracle Database naming restrictions, what is the maximum length permitted for a table or column name?
questions.e: Table and column names may contain up to 30 alphanumeric characters. They must also start with a letter, avoid spaces and most special characters, and avoid reserved words.

questions.q: Within which scope must a table name be unique in Oracle Database?
questions.e: Table names must be unique within a schema. By contrast, column names must be unique within a table, which is the commonly confused rule.

questions.q: Within which scope must a column name be unique in Oracle Database?
questions.e: Column names must be unique within a table. Table names, on the other hand, must be unique within a schema.

questions.q: Which of the following must table and column names avoid, according to Oracle Database naming restrictions?
questions.e: Table and column names must avoid reserved words. They are allowed to use letters and alphanumeric characters; in fact names must start with a letter.

questions.q: In Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler, what is a glossary?
o: A set of accepted terms that can be used in the design
A list of every row stored in a table
questions.e: A glossary is a set of accepted terms that can be used in the design, ensuring the model complies with set naming standards when engineering between the logical and relational models. It is not a data listing or an ERD.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of creating a glossary directly from an existing logical model rather than building a new glossary from scratch?
o: It automatically enforces Oracle reserved-word rules
Entity and attribute names from the logical model are added automatically
It removes the need to engineer the model
It creates the primary key constraints for you
questions.e: Creating a glossary from an existing logical model is quicker and easier because the entity and attribute names from the model are added automatically. It does not replace the engineering step or generate constraints.

questions.q: Before any glossary is applied, how are table names produced by default when a logical model is engineered to a relational model in Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler?
o: As plurals of the entity names
Mapped directly from the entity names and not as plurals
With all spaces removed and capitalized
questions.e: By default, table names are mapped directly from entity names and are not plurals; producing plural table names requires applying a glossary. Column names by default come directly from attribute names with spaces replaced by underscores.

questions.q: Before a glossary is applied, how are column names produced by default from attribute names during engineering?
o: Mapped as the plural of each attribute name
Replaced entirely by table short names
Mapped directly from attribute names, except that spaces are replaced by underscores
questions.e: By default, column names are mapped directly from attribute names, with the exception that spaces are replaced by underscores. Abbreviations from a glossary are only applied once the glossary is used as the naming standard.

questions.q: When a glossary is created from a logical model, what does the Glossary editor automatically suggest for the terms?
questions.e: The Glossary editor includes suggested plurals and abbreviations, which can be edited or deleted. It does not generate constraints or data types.

questions.q: For a saved glossary to actually be applied during engineering, where must it be added in Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler?
o: On the Naming Standard page in the Preferences dialog box
On the Subtypes tab of the entity
questions.e: The glossary must be added on the Naming Standard page in the Preferences (Properties) dialog box for it to be applied during engineering. The Templates page is instead used for constraint-name patterns.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes a physical model in Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler?
o: It is the same thing as the conceptual model
It is the blueprint for the actual database implementation and is known as a Relational Model
It cannot be adapted to an RDBMS
questions.e: A physical model is the blueprint for the actual database implementation, can be the basis for any type of DBMS, and in Data Modeler is known as a Relational Model. The ideal model can be adapted to an RDBMS model.

questions.q: After the glossary naming standards are applied, how are singular entity names mapped to table names?
o: They are mapped to their abbreviations
They are mapped to primary key names
They are mapped to plural table names
questions.e: By applying the naming standards contained in the glossary, singular entity names in the logical model are mapped to plural table names in the relational model. Without the glossary, the default table names are not plurals.

questions.q: If terms such as Publisher and Transaction are included in attribute names, what happens when the glossary naming standards are applied?
o: The abbreviations specified for those terms are applied in the column names
The full terms are kept in the column names
questions.e: When the glossary naming standards are applied, the abbreviations specified for terms like Publisher and Transaction are applied within the column names. The glossary maps entity names to table names and applies attribute abbreviations to column names.

questions.q: How is a primary key constraint named under the recommended naming convention?
o: Using the full table name followed by PK
Using the short table name, an underscore, and the suffix PK
Using the short table names of both tables and the suffix FK
Using the referenced column name and the suffix UID
questions.e: Primary key constraints are named using the short table name, an underscore, and the suffix PK. The both-tables-plus-FK pattern is used for foreign key constraints, not primary key constraints.

questions.q: How is a foreign key constraint named under the recommended naming convention?
o: Using the short table name of one table and the suffix PK
Using only the referenced column name and the suffix FK
Using the short table names of both tables, an underscore, and the suffix FK
Using the full table name and the suffix CK
questions.e: Foreign key constraints are named using the short table names of both tables, an underscore, and the suffix FK. A single short table name with the PK suffix describes a primary key constraint instead.

questions.q: How is a foreign key column named under the recommended naming convention?
o: Using the short table names of both tables and the suffix FK
Using the short table name and the suffix PK
Using the referenced table's full name and the suffix CK
Using the short table name and column name of the table the foreign key references
questions.e: Foreign key columns are named using the short table name and column name of the table the foreign key references. The both-tables-plus-FK form describes the foreign key constraint, not the foreign key column.

questions.q: Why should database constraints be given meaningful names?
o: To allow them to be easily referenced
To reduce the number of tables
questions.e: Constraints should be given meaningful names so that they can be easily referenced. Constraints themselves enforce rules and ensure the consistency and integrity of the database.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of constraints in a database?
o: To enforce rules and ensure the consistency and integrity of the database
questions.e: Constraints enforce rules and ensure the consistency and integrity of the database. Giving them meaningful names is a separate concern that makes them easier to reference.

questions.q: By default, what does Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler use to build constraint names, and what problem can this cause?
o: The short table name, which can be too vague
The column data type, which can be ambiguous
The full table name, which can produce names that are long and may exceed the maximum permitted SQL characters
A random identifier, which is hard to read
questions.e: By default, constraint names are created using the full table name, which can lead to very long names that are hard to manage and may exceed the maximum permitted number of characters in SQL. Applying abbreviations shortens them.

questions.q: To apply naming standards to constraint names via abbreviations, what must first be created?
o: A .csv file in a spreadsheet application
questions.e: To apply naming standards to constraint names, you first create a .csv file in a spreadsheet application listing table names and their abbreviations. This file is then referenced when applying name abbreviations.

questions.q: In the .csv file used for constraint-name abbreviations, what belongs in the first and second columns?
o: First: full (plural) table names; Second: the abbreviation to use
First: abbreviations; Second: full table names
First: column names; Second: data types
First: primary keys; Second: foreign keys
questions.e: In the abbreviation .csv file, the first column specifies the full (plural) table names and the second column specifies the abbreviation to use for each. The file is saved as .csv and its location is noted for later use.

questions.q: When defining a naming template so constraint names use abbreviated table names, what must be added to the pattern?
questions.e: You edit the template to use abbreviated names for Primary and Foreign keys and the Column Foreign Key by adding abbr to the pattern. This makes the template reference the abbreviation rather than the full table name.

questions.q: Which menu path applies the abbreviations from the naming template to the model?
questions.e: To apply the abbreviations you select Tools and then Name Abbreviations, browse to the .csv file, and click OK. This is distinct from the Templates page, which only defines the pattern.

questions.q: When applying name abbreviations, why would you un-check the Tables option?
o: To rename the columns to their data types
To maintain the existing table names from the glossary
questions.e: You un-check Tables so that the existing table names from the glossary are maintained, letting the abbreviations affect only the constraint names. Leaving it checked would let the abbreviation process also rename the tables.

questions.q: Which of the following are the two ways subtypes can be mapped to tables?
o: One table (single table implementation) and two table (a table for each child subtype)
One column per subtype and one row per subtype
A view for each subtype and a synonym for each subtype
A primary key table and a foreign key table
questions.e: Subtypes can be mapped either as one table (a single table implementation) or as two tables (a table for each child subtype). These are the subtype-to-table mapping options, not column, view, or key based schemes.

questions.q: In Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler, how do you select the method used to engineer subtypes?
o: Right-click the relational model and choose Engineer
Double-click the supertype entity, select Subtypes, and choose a method from the Subtree generation dropdown
questions.e: You double-click the supertype entity to edit its properties, select Subtypes, and choose the required method from the Subtree generation dropdown. This is separate from the constraint-abbreviation workflow.

questions.q: When naming standards are applied, unique identifiers (UIDs) are mapped to which relational structures?
questions.e: Applying the naming standards maps UIDs to primary key constraints. Relationships, by contrast, are mapped to foreign key columns and constraints.

questions.q: When naming standards are applied, relationships are mapped to which relational structures?
questions.e: Relationships are mapped to foreign key columns and constraints. UIDs instead map to primary key constraints, which is the common point of confusion.

questions.q: Which suffix is used when naming a primary key constraint?
questions.e: Primary key constraints use the suffix PK, combined with the short table name and an underscore. The FK suffix is reserved for foreign key constraints.

questions.q: Which suffix is used when naming a foreign key constraint?
questions.e: Foreign key constraints use the suffix FK, combined with the short table names of both tables and an underscore. The PK suffix is used for primary key constraints instead.

questions.q: How many table short names are combined when forming a foreign key constraint name?
o: Two (the short table names of both tables)
None; the full column name is used
questions.e: A foreign key constraint name combines the short table names of both tables, plus an underscore and the FK suffix. Using a single short table name with a suffix describes a primary key constraint or a foreign key column instead.

questions.q: If the logical model has already been engineered, what may sometimes be necessary before applying the naming abbreviations correctly?
o: Recreate the logical model from scratch
Convert the model to a conceptual model first
Delete all objects in the relational model, re-engineer the logical model, then apply the naming abbreviations
questions.e: Sometimes it is necessary to delete all objects in the relational model, re-engineer the logical model, and then apply the naming abbreviations so the constraint names follow the standards. The logical model itself does not need to be recreated.

questions.q: Where in Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler do you set the pattern used for constraint naming?
o: Right-click the Design, Properties, expand Settings and Naming Standard, then select Templates
The Subtypes tab of the supertype entity
questions.e: The naming pattern for constraints is set on the Templates page: right-click the Design in the Object Browser, select Properties, expand Settings and Naming Standard, then select Templates. The Glossary Editor handles table and column term names, not constraint patterns.

questions.q: A person checks email or has a grocery clerk scan an item to calculate a bill, using a fully developed, ready-to-use program without knowing how it works internally. This kind of program is best classified as which type of software?
questions.e: A ready-to-use program the end user interacts with (email, point-of-sale) is application software. System software runs the underlying operations of the machine and is not what the end user directly buys to accomplish a task.

questions.q: What kind of tool is Oracle Application Express (APEX)?
o: An operating system for the database server
A web application development, deployment, and maintenance tool
A spreadsheet program for storing data
A database backup and recovery utility
questions.e: Oracle Application Express is described as a web application development, deployment, and maintenance tool. It is not a backup utility, an operating system, or a spreadsheet.
